sources.title: Chrome can now pull autofill suggestions straight from Gmail - Android Authority
passages: Autofill has always been a reliable Chrome companion, but it has largely been limited to handling the basics, like your name, address, and credit card number.
With Gemini and Personal Intelligence now in the mix, the feature can finally tap into your Gmail account to pull relevant information when you’re filling out online forms.
That doesn’t necessarily mean the enhanced autofill feature will leverage your Gmail data for targeted ads, but it sure does raise questions.
The company, for its part, said all your sensitive Gmail data accessed by autofill remains encrypted.
Plus, you get to decide whether to enable the feature and what it “can access via your Chrome settings.”

Note that in its initial Canary implementation, the feature could pull information from Gmail, Google Photos, and “other connected apps.” In its current stable implementation, enhanced autofill appears to be limited to Gmail.
Would you let Chrome's Gemini-powered autofill access your Gmail?
Whenever you tap on a text field and a suggestion is available, it will appear under a Suggested by Gemini section.
Tapping the suggestion, as seen in the example above, highlights its source.

Google Chrome’s autofill is getting eager to help you out — a little too eager, if you ask us. Earlier this year, the tech giant started testing a feature that would let Gemini fill out forms in Chrome with information from across your Google account. Now, the company is bringing a more stable version of that functionality to a lot more users.

For reference, when we reported on the development earlier this year, the autofill update was limited to Chrome Canary. Fast-forward to today, and it’s rolling out to all Gemini Personal Intelligence users in the US.

Autofill has always been a reliable Chrome companion, but it has largely been limited to handling the basics, like your name, address, and credit card number. With Gemini and Personal Intelligence now in the mix, the feature can finally tap into your Gmail account to pull relevant information when you’re filling out online forms.

Note that in its initial Canary implementation, the feature could pull information from Gmail, Google Photos, and “other connected apps.” In its current stable implementation, enhanced autofill appears to be limited to Gmail.

According to Google, the enhanced experience will surface order numbers, package tracking details, and flight bookings directly from Gmail whenever you need them. So, next time you’re trying to check in online for an upcoming flight, you won’t have to dig through your inbox to find your booking code or ticket number, as shown in the short GIF above.
Similarly, if you’re trying to track down a FedEx package, the feature would be able to autofill relevant tracking numbers for you.

Whenever you tap on a text field and a suggestion is available, it will appear under a Suggested by Gemini section. Tapping the suggestion, as seen in the example above, highlights its source. This suggests that the feature could extend beyond Gmail. Lastly, this is also where you’ll be able to remove the suggestion in question or jump right into Chrome’s enhanced autofill settings to manage the feature.

Of course, this level of convenience comes with privacy concerns, especially considering how much sensitive information our inboxes tend to store. And those concerns aren’t even unfounded. Just last week, we reported on an updated Google policy that states the company can use data shared through Personal Intelligence to personalize ads displayed to you.

That doesn’t necessarily mean the enhanced autofill feature will leverage your Gmail data for targeted ads, but it sure does raise questions. The company, for its part, said all your sensitive Gmail data accessed by autofill remains encrypted. Plus, you get to decide whether to enable the feature and what it “can access via your Chrome settings.”
Google didn’t offer a look at how these privacy controls work, and since the feature hasn’t landed for us just yet, we haven’t been able to explore them either.

We’ll have to wait until the feature becomes available to get a clearer picture of exactly how much control users have over the feature. Enhanced autofill is now rolling out to Personal Intelligence users in the US on desktop, Android, and iOS.
Would you let Chrome's Gemini-powered autofill access your Gmail?

extraction.body: Following improvements made to Chrome’s enhanced autofill last year that included your name, passport number, email address, and physical addresses sourced from your Google Accounts and services like Google Wallet, the feature is now expanding. Starting today, Chrome’s enhanced autofill will use Gemini with Personal Intelligence to suggest information sourced from your Gmail, potentially saving you from having to search for confirmation emails, receipts, or shipping updates yourself. The expanded autofill capabilities can retrieve details such as a shipment’s tracking number, travel details like a flight booking number or hotel reservation, or the order number of a recent purchase. They’ll be available through Gemini in Chrome for users with Personal Intelligence turned on in the desktop, Android, and iOS versions of the browser.

Earlier this year, the tech giant started testing a feature that would let Gemini fill out forms in Chrome with information from across your Google account. Now, the company is bringing a more stable version of that functionality to a lot more users.

For reference, when we reported on the development earlier this year, the autofill update was limited to Chrome Canary. Fast-forward to today, and it’s rolling out to all Gemini Personal Intelligence users in the US.

Autofill has always been a reliable Chrome companion, but it has largely been limited to handling the basics, like your name, address, and credit card number. With Gemini and Personal Intelligence now in the mix, the feature can finally tap into your Gmail account to pull relevant information when you’re filling out online forms.

Note that in its initial Canary implementation, the feature could pull information from Gmail, Google Photos, and “other connected apps.” In its current stable implementation, enhanced autofill appears to be limited to Gmail.

According to Google, the enhanced experience will surface order numbers, package tracking details, and flight bookings directly from Gmail whenever you need them. So, next time you’re trying to check in online for an upcoming flight, you won’t have to dig through your inbox to find your booking code or ticket number, as shown in the short GIF above.
Similarly, if you’re trying to track down a FedEx package, the feature would be able to autofill relevant tracking numbers for you.

Whenever you tap on a text field and a suggestion is available, it will appear under a Suggested by Gemini section. Tapping the suggestion, as seen in the example above, highlights its source. This suggests that the feature could extend beyond Gmail. Lastly, this is also where you’ll be able to remove the suggestion in question or jump right into Chrome’s enhanced autofill settings to manage the feature.

Of course, this level of convenience comes with privacy concerns, especially considering how much sensitive information our inboxes tend to store. And those concerns aren’t even unfounded. Just last week, we reported on an updated Google policy that states the company can use data shared through Personal Intelligence to personalize ads displayed to you.

That doesn’t necessarily mean the enhanced autofill feature will leverage your Gmail data for targeted ads, but it sure does raise questions. The company, for its part, said all your sensitive Gmail data accessed by autofill remains encrypted. Plus, you get to decide whether to enable the feature and what it “can access via your Chrome settings.”
Google didn’t offer a look at how these privacy controls work, and since the feature hasn’t landed for us just yet, we haven’t been able to explore them either.

passages: After months of rumors and speculation , Apple just announced its latest entry-level addition to its MacBook lineup: the MacBook Neo.

Priced at $599 and equipped with an A18 processor (the same chip found in the iPhone 16 Pro), Apple takes aim at budget PCs and Chromebooks in the low-end PC market — an area in which it historically has had virtually no market share.
In fact, the Neo, with its current hardware and ecosystem-based software, can give similarly priced Dell, HP, Acer, and other Windows laptops a good run for their money.

passages: Alongside the teasers, Apple has also sent media invites for an experience in LA on October 28, 2026.
That’s the same wording the company used to describe its ‘Welcome Home’ event, so I’d suspect there won’t be a formal keynote, but there will be plenty of hands-on time.
However, Joswiak’s post teases something Pro that could be on the horizon.
There’s been no shortage of rumors, and it’s likely that Apple will drop a significant update to the MacBook Pro family next week, finally delivering a touchscreen laptop.
Either way, we only have a few more days to wait to see what Apple has been working on.
After all, the company has promised to ‘Pro and Tell.’ Let me know what you’re most excited about in the comments below.
Recent reports also hint that the M6 could be coming to the iMac , which is due for an upgrade after launching with the M4 in 2024.

Both the new 14-inch and 16-inch models are expected to pair the first touchscreen on a Mac with an OLED display, delivering the same vibrant, rich viewing experience as an OLED iPhone or iPad Pro, all within a redesigned, slimmer notebook.

Coming shortly after the iPhone Duo starts shipping, a major iPad mini upgrade is also rumored.

Apple ’s on a roll! Just eight days after dropping the HomeView , HomePod mini 2 , and Apple TV 4K , and four days before the iPhone Duo starts shipping, the Cupertino-based technology giant is teasing more. In a post on X (formerly Twitter) , Apple’s SVP of Marketing, Greg Joswiak, writes, “Can’t wait to pro and tell next week,” alongside an Apple logo being drawn. The same graphic was also posted to @HelloApple on Instagram with the caption, “About next week…” The latter gives us the timing and leaves us marking our calendars for a reveal similar to Apple’s recent home product launches. However, Joswiak’s post teases something Pro that could be on the horizon. Alongside the teasers, Apple has also sent media invites for an experience in LA on October 28, 2026. That’s the same wording the company used to describe its ‘Welcome Home’ event, so I’d suspect there won’t be a formal keynote, but there will be plenty of hands-on time. The teaser depicts the Apple logo being drawn using an array of colors, mostly silver, white, and blue, with small, vibrant pops of red, orange, and yellow. To me, it looks as though a finger could be drawing the logo, given the overall shape, or perhaps a brush of some sort is being used to create it. Either way, it points to the likely arrival of new Macs or iPads. Remember, like most of Apple’s products, these devices feature an Apple logo on the back. There’s been no shortage of rumors, and it’s likely that Apple will drop a significant update to the MacBook Pro family next week, finally delivering a touchscreen laptop. That’s something the company has been pretty firm about ruling out, but it seems to have turned a corner if recent reports are to be believed. Both the new 14-inch and 16-inch models are expected to pair the first touchscreen on a Mac with an OLED display, delivering the same vibrant, rich viewing experience as an OLED iPhone or iPad Pro, all within a redesigned, slimmer notebook. Under the hood, these flagship MacBooks will likely get Apple’s best chips, whether that’s the M6 or the M5 Ultra, which premiered with the Mac mini and Mac Studio in August 2026. Recent reports also hint that the M6 could be coming to the iMac , which is due for an upgrade after launching with the M4 in 2024. A new entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro could also arrive with a design similar to the current generation, likely featuring the M6 chip instead of the M5 for better performance across the board, particularly for AI tasks. Alongside the Mac, the iPad could also be in the mix, potentially hinted at by the vibrant colors and what appears to be a finer, brush-drawn Apple logo. Coming shortly after the iPhone Duo starts shipping, a major iPad mini upgrade is also rumored. It could carry a considerably higher price — a reminder that the current model starts at $699 / £699 / AU$949 — and add a ProMotion OLED display, a redesigned body, and a more capable chip under the hood. I’ve been wishing for a redesigned iPad mini with Magic Keyboard support and a better screen for a while, so this would be music to my ears, and likely to many others’ too. The iPad lineup is still in pretty good shape, with the Air and Pro models already receiving updates with better processors earlier this year. Besides the iPad mini, the only other model likely due for an upgrade is the entry-level iPad, but it’s unclear whether it will be updated next week. Either way, we only have a few more days to wait to see what Apple has been working on. After all, the company has promised to ‘Pro and Tell.’ Let me know what you’re most excited about in the comments below. coreStoryFacts.text: After months of rumors and speculation , Apple just announced its latest entry-level addition to its MacBook lineup: the MacBook Neo.

Priced at $599 and equipped with an A18 processor (the same chip found in the iPhone 16 Pro), Apple takes aim at budget PCs and Chromebooks in the low-end PC market — an area in which it historically has had virtually no market share.
In fact, the Neo, with its current hardware and ecosystem-based software, can give similarly priced Dell, HP, Acer, and other Windows laptops a good run for their money.
Having continuity features with the iPhone, alone, may convinced existing PC users to make the switch.

As the entry-level device in its laptop lineup, Apple’s recently announced MacBook Air M5 and MacBook Pro and Pro Max M5 saw price increases of $100 to $400, pushing those models further into premium territory to make room for the affordable Neo.
Sure, the iMac M4 dropped in a handful of fun colorways, but the laptops specifically have been steadfastly monotone for too long.

This is something Apple used to be known for, after all — lightness and accessibility.
Alongside the teasers, Apple has also sent media invites for an experience in LA on October 28, 2026.
That’s the same wording the company used to describe its ‘Welcome Home’ event, so I’d suspect there won’t be a formal keynote, but there will be plenty of hands-on time.
However, Joswiak’s post teases something Pro that could be on the horizon.
There’s been no shortage of rumors, and it’s likely that Apple will drop a significant update to the MacBook Pro family next week, finally delivering a touchscreen laptop.
Either way, we only have a few more days to wait to see what Apple has been working on.
After all, the company has promised to ‘Pro and Tell.’ Let me know what you’re most excited about in the comments below.
Recent reports also hint that the M6 could be coming to the iMac , which is due for an upgrade after launching with the M4 in 2024.

Both the new 14-inch and 16-inch models are expected to pair the first touchscreen on a Mac with an OLED display, delivering the same vibrant, rich viewing experience as an OLED iPhone or iPad Pro, all within a redesigned, slimmer notebook.
Alongside the Mac, the iPad could also be in the mix, potentially hinted at by the vibrant colors and what appears to be a finer, brush-drawn Apple logo.
Coming shortly after the iPhone Duo starts shipping, a major iPad mini upgrade is also rumored.
Jacob Krol is the US Managing Editor, News for TechRadar.
I’ve been wishing for a redesigned iPad mini with Magic Keyboard support and a better screen for a while, so this would be music to my ears, and likely to many others’ too.

Apple ’s on a roll! Just eight days after dropping the HomeView , HomePod mini 2 , and Apple TV 4K , and four days before the iPhone Duo starts shipping, the Cupertino-based technology giant is teasing more. In a post on X (formerly Twitter) , Apple’s SVP of Marketing, Greg Joswiak, writes, “Can’t wait to pro and tell next week,” alongside an Apple logo being drawn. The same graphic was also posted to @HelloApple on Instagram with the caption, “About next week…” The latter gives us the timing and leaves us marking our calendars for a reveal similar to Apple’s recent home product launches. However, Joswiak’s post teases something Pro that could be on the horizon. Alongside the teasers, Apple has also sent media invites for an experience in LA on October 28, 2026. That’s the same wording the company used to describe its ‘Welcome Home’ event, so I’d suspect there won’t be a formal keynote, but there will be plenty of hands-on time. The teaser depicts the Apple logo being drawn using an array of colors, mostly silver, white, and blue, with small, vibrant pops of red, orange, and yellow. To me, it looks as though a finger could be drawing the logo, given the overall shape, or perhaps a brush of some sort is being used to create it. Either way, it points to the likely arrival of new Macs or iPads. Remember, like most of Apple’s products, these devices feature an Apple logo on the back. There’s been no shortage of rumors, and it’s likely that Apple will drop a significant update to the MacBook Pro family next week, finally delivering a touchscreen laptop. That’s something the company has been pretty firm about ruling out, but it seems to have turned a corner if recent reports are to be believed. Both the new 14-inch and 16-inch models are expected to pair the first touchscreen on a Mac with an OLED display, delivering the same vibrant, rich viewing experience as an OLED iPhone or iPad Pro, all within a redesigned, slimmer notebook. Under the hood, these flagship MacBooks will likely get Apple’s best chips, whether that’s the M6 or the M5 Ultra, which premiered with the Mac mini and Mac Studio in August 2026. Recent reports also hint that the M6 could be coming to the iMac , which is due for an upgrade after launching with the M4 in 2024. A new entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro could also arrive with a design similar to the current generation, likely featuring the M6 chip instead of the M5 for better performance across the board, particularly for AI tasks. Alongside the Mac, the iPad could also be in the mix, potentially hinted at by the vibrant colors and what appears to be a finer, brush-drawn Apple logo. Coming shortly after the iPhone Duo starts shipping, a major iPad mini upgrade is also rumored. It could carry a considerably higher price — a reminder that the current model starts at $699 / £699 / AU$949 — and add a ProMotion OLED display, a redesigned body, and a more capable chip under the hood. I’ve been wishing for a redesigned iPad mini with Magic Keyboard support and a better screen for a while, so this would be music to my ears, and likely to many others’ too. The iPad lineup is still in pretty good shape, with the Air and Pro models already receiving updates with better processors earlier this year. Besides the iPad mini, the only other model likely due for an upgrade is the entry-level iPad, but it’s unclear whether it will be updated next week. Either way, we only have a few more days to wait to see what Apple has been working on. After all, the company has promised to ‘Pro and Tell.’ Let me know what you’re most excited about in the comments below. sources.title: Hands-on with Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro
passages: The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display weighs just 3 pounds, which is noticeably lighter than the current generation of non-touch MacBook Pros, which start at 3.4 pounds for the newly introduced M6 models.
Touch works almost exactly like you’d expect it to with Apple’s first-party apps.
Steve Jobs famously called touchscreen laptops “ergonomically terrible,” and for over a decade, Apple stridently refused to make one.
Today that all changes with the MacBook Pro — the company’s first laptop to embrace a touch interface.
While it’s unlikely that Apple can fix all the “terrible” ergonomics of having to lift your arm up and touch a laptop screen, the company has put some effort into making macOS more touch-friendly.

It’s a seemingly minor feature, but one that definitely got the audience excited during the introduction, and marks the return of a bit of flair to the MacBook lineup which, let’s be fair, has grown a bit utilitarian-looking over the years. Touch works almost exactly like you’d expect it to with Apple’s first-party apps. That being said, anyone who has tried to “click” on a tiny button in an app with their finger knows that a pretty fiddly experience, at best, and infuriating at worst. Unsurprisingly, there is a price premium for the new MacBook Pro PROLED XDR. The touchscreen OLED model starts at $2,899, $400 more than the otherwise similarly-specced M5 Pro MacBook Pro.

In the video, the Touch Bar is used to display notifications and status updates from applications installed on the notebook
Obviously this MacBook Pro is unofficial, however it is based on industry rumours.

Given that Apple is tipped to be rolling-out its Face ID technology to more and more products across its line-up, it makes sense the system will eventually land on the MacBook Pro range in the near future.

It also marks the long-requested return of the glowing Apple logo on the lid. It starts at $2,899 for the 14-inch model and $3,399 for the 16-inch model, and preorders start today, with deliveries beginning November 6. Today’s announcement follows yesterday’s unveiling of the M6-powered iMac and 14-inch MacBook Pro , both of which are also set to become available on November 6. Stay tuned for 9to5Mac’s full coverage of today’s announcement. Are you getting the new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display? Let us know in the comments. Back in March, Apple upgraded the standard 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro laptops to the current M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.
MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time, bringing pros a whole new way to interact with their content.
Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined.

Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place.
And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself.
Apple also touts the use of a new hinge technology in the MacBook Pro, in part to support touch input without compromising on stability:

The new machines still use Touch ID with no Face ID support.
We’ll have to keep waiting for Face ID and built-in cellular connectivity.

Apple’s Mac lineup consists of MacBook, MacBoo…

In addition, a newly designed hinge provides greater stability while using Touch, and advanced video stabilization automatically smooths the camera feed in real time while using Touch on a video call.

extraction.body: Apple has officially announced the all-new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display, its first touchscreen laptop. The new machine was first hinted at by Apple on October 19 with the company’s “Pro and tell” experience teaser . Earlier today, new Apple CEO John Ternus shared a “spotlight” teaser for the laptop as well. Read on for all the details about the new high-end laptop… The new machine features a light-up Apple logo, tandem OLED, and touch input on the display. It runs on the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, like the existing MacBook Pro models without OLED touch displays. John Ternus, who is rocking a new profile picture with the new Mac, shared the first look at the new machine on X: We’re glowing with excitement over the new MacBook Pro. You’ve gotta touch it to believe it. pic.twitter.com/BLiGkGaefL Apple previously used a glowing Apple logo on its notebook hardware for years until the 12-inch MacBook and 2016 MacBook Pro. Pricing for the new laptop starts at $2899 for the 14-inch model. The 16-inch version starts at $3399. Pre-orders are available starting today with deliveries starting November 6. You can find the product page for the new MacBook Pro here . Colors include silver or space black options with standard or nano-texture display configurations. Beyond the new high-end laptop, Apple also announced the redesigned iPad mini , M6 iMac , and M6 14-inch MacBook Pro this week. Back in March, Apple upgraded the standard 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro laptops to the current M5 Pro and M5 Max chips. Apple calls the new design both thinner and lighter than the standard MacBook Pro models in the same size configuration. The new MacBook Pro is the first to use what Apple calls a PROLED XDR display, replacing Mini-LED as the MacBook Pro display technology. While Apple has innovated with multi-touch on the iPhone and iPad, the Mac has been resistant to touch input for years. The new MacBook Pro changes that with the first touchscreen Mac display. Here’s what Apple says about touch on the Mac. MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time, bringing pros a whole new way to interact with their content. Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined. Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place. And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself. Apple also touts the use of a new hinge technology in the MacBook Pro, in part to support touch input without compromising on stability: Touch also introduces entirely new ways of working for pro users. Graphic designers can now use the entire display as their canvas, no longer constrained by the area of the trackpad when drawing; musicians can play software instruments right onscreen; and app developers can test how Touch performs in their iOS and iPadOS apps directly on the MacBook Pro display. And these new ways to interact with MacBook Pro work in tandem with the keyboard shortcuts and trackpad gestures pros know and love. In addition, a newly designed hinge provides greater stability while using Touch, and advanced video stabilization automatically smooths the camera feed in real time while using Touch on a video call. In addition to touch as an additional input method, the new MacBook Pro also adopts the Dynamic Island in favor of the notch. The Dynamic Island now comes to Mac, serving as the home for Spotlight, Live Activities, and Siri AI. Not interested in touch? The existing MacBook Pro configurations from March stick around at the same prices. You just lose OLED, the glowing Apple logo, and the thinner and lighter design. Performance, however, is pretty much on par between versions as both offer M5 Pro and M5 Max chips. The new laptops can be configured with up to 128GB of unified memory and 16TB of solid state drive storage. The 14-inch model is half a pound lighter at just 3 pounds even compared to 3.5 pounds for the same version of the previous design. The overall footprint is reduced as well with 0.59 x 12.24 x 8.52 inch dimensions compared to 0.61 x 12.31 x 8.71 inch dimensions when comparing 14-inch models. passages: Apple has officially announced the all-new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display, its first touchscreen laptop.

The new machine was first hinted at by Apple on October 19 with the company’s “Pro and tell” experience teaser . Earlier today, new Apple CEO John Ternus shared a “spotlight” teaser for the laptop as well.
Read on for all the details about the new high-end laptop…
The new machine features a light-up Apple logo, tandem OLED, and touch input on the display.
It runs on the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, like the existing MacBook Pro models without OLED touch displays.
John Ternus, who is rocking a new profile picture with the new Mac, shared the first look at the new machine on X:
We’re glowing with excitement over the new MacBook Pro. You’ve gotta touch it to believe it. pic.twitter.com/BLiGkGaefL
Apple previously used a glowing Apple logo on its notebook hardware for years until the 12-inch MacBook and 2016 MacBook Pro.
Pricing for the new laptop starts at $2899 for the 14-inch model. The 16-inch version starts at $3399.
Pre-orders are available starting today with deliveries starting November 6. You can find the product page for the new MacBook Pro here .
Colors include silver or space black options with standard or nano-texture display configurations.

Beyond the new high-end laptop, Apple also announced the redesigned iPad mini , M6 iMac , and M6 14-inch MacBook Pro this week. Back in March, Apple upgraded the standard 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro laptops to the current M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.
Apple calls the new design both thinner and lighter than the standard MacBook Pro models in the same size configuration.
The new MacBook Pro is the first to use what Apple calls a PROLED XDR display, replacing Mini-LED as the MacBook Pro display technology.

While Apple has innovated with multi-touch on the iPhone and iPad, the Mac has been resistant to touch input for years. The new MacBook Pro changes that with the first touchscreen Mac display. Here’s what Apple says about touch on the Mac.

MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time, bringing pros a whole new way to interact with their content. Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined. Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place. And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself.
Apple also touts the use of a new hinge technology in the MacBook Pro, in part to support touch input without compromising on stability:

Touch also introduces entirely new ways of working for pro users. Graphic designers can now use the entire display as their canvas, no longer constrained by the area of the trackpad when drawing; musicians can play software instruments right onscreen; and app developers can test how Touch performs in their iOS and iPadOS apps directly on the MacBook Pro display. And these new ways to interact with MacBook Pro work in tandem with the keyboard shortcuts and trackpad gestures pros know and love. In addition, a newly designed hinge provides greater stability while using Touch, and advanced video stabilization automatically smooths the camera feed in real time while using Touch on a video call.
In addition to touch as an additional input method, the new MacBook Pro also adopts the Dynamic Island in favor of the notch.
The Dynamic Island now comes to Mac, serving as the home for Spotlight, Live Activities, and Siri AI.

Not interested in touch? The existing MacBook Pro configurations from March stick around at the same prices. You just lose OLED, the glowing Apple logo, and the thinner and lighter design. Performance, however, is pretty much on par between versions as both offer M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.
The new laptops can be configured with up to 128GB of unified memory and 16TB of solid state drive storage.

The 16-inch model is notably lighter as well. The new design weighs in at 4 pounds even compared to 4.7 pounds for the previous design. Dimensions change to 0.63 x 14 x 9.62 inches compared to 0.66 x 14.01 x 9.77 inches between designs.
Playing piano on the touchscreen MacBook Pro pic.twitter.com/lDlwIeqErd

The new machines still use Touch ID with no Face ID support. Apple also doesn’t offer built-in cellular models of the new MacBook Pro. We’ll have to keep waiting for Face ID and built-in cellular connectivity.

passages: LOS ANGELES—Apple today announced and gave a first glimpse of its first major MacBook Pro redesign in more than five years.
As rumored, it includes an OLED display and, for the first time on macOS, a touchscreen—a change Apple has long debated. (Former CEO Steve Jobs famously was opposed.)

The OLED display (which Apple is, of course, calling the PROLED XDR) seems to be the real highlight here, compared to earlier models: It can achieve 2,000 nits in terms of maximum brightness, and Apple says it has a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.
References were made to burn-in protection, but details on which approach it’s taking for that weren’t yet shared.
The display retains the 120Hz variable refresh rate of its predecessors.
Memory configurations top out at the same places they did in the previous MacBook Pro models with M5 Max: up to 128 GB of RAM.
That said, storage can now go up to 16 TB—if you can afford it.
Beyond that, the design is largely similar to the existing one, but there are a few notable differences.
Apple said when announcing it that the 14-inch model is just 3 pounds, down around half a pound from the previous model, depending on configuration.

The M6 series has already arrived in other Macs, but it seems Apple is skipping them for this refresh; there were previously reports that Apple planned to hold off on updating the chip until the M7 series, which could have significant improvements for AI performance, just like the recently released A20 Pro chip for the iPhone does.
Second, the top-of-screen camera notch has been replaced by the small black cutout that Apple calls the Dynamic Island.
Presumably it works similarly to the one we’ve seen on the iPhone, expanding or contracting to show live activities and other information.

LOS ANGELES—Apple today announced and gave a first glimpse of its first major MacBook Pro redesign in more than five years. As rumored, it includes an OLED display and, for the first time on macOS, a touchscreen—a change Apple has long debated. (Former CEO Steve Jobs famously was opposed.)

Apple’s demonstration video showed users interacting with applications by reaching up to touch the screen, including file dragging and multi-touch gestures like pinch-to-zoom. It does not appear to be a 2-in-1 convertible design, though; all the footage was of people reaching up to touch the screen in a normal laptop configuration.

The OLED display (which Apple is, of course, calling the PROLED XDR) seems to be the real highlight here, compared to earlier models: It can achieve 2,000 nits in terms of maximum brightness, and Apple says it has a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. References were made to burn-in protection, but details on which approach it’s taking for that weren’t yet shared. The display retains the 120Hz variable refresh rate of its predecessors.

Beyond that, the design is largely similar to the existing one, but there are a few notable differences. First, it’s much lighter. Apple said when announcing it that the 14-inch model is just 3 pounds, down around half a pound from the previous model, depending on configuration.

Second, the top-of-screen camera notch has been replaced by the small black cutout that Apple calls the Dynamic Island. Presumably it works similarly to the one we’ve seen on the iPhone, expanding or contracting to show live activities and other information.
Finally, there’s a retro throwback: The Apple logo on the back of the lid glows like the logo on MacBooks of yore.

In terms of specs, this refresh includes the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips—the same ones in the previous refresh. The M6 series has already arrived in other Macs, but it seems Apple is skipping them for this refresh; there were previously reports that Apple planned to hold off on updating the chip until the M7 series, which could have significant improvements for AI performance, just like the recently released A20 Pro chip for the iPhone does.
Memory configurations top out at the same places they did in the previous MacBook Pro models with M5 Max: up to 128 GB of RAM. That said, storage can now go up to 16 TB—if you can afford it.

Preorders start today, and the device will reach consumers on November 6. As expected, the price is the catch. The M5 Pro-equipped 14-inch model starts at $2899, while the 16-inch starts at $3,399. But if you want the M5 Max, you’re looking at a $4,499 starting point for the 14-inch, and $4,799 for the 16-inch—and that’s not accounting for any potential RAM or storage upgrades.

Apple announced an all-new MacBook Pro laptop with an OLED touchscreen at its “Pro and tell” event on Wednesday.
The 14-inch model weighs 3 pounds, and the 16-inch model weighs 4 pounds, according to Apple.

In a press release, Apple said its apps are optimized for touch and that an updated API will let developers add touch to their own apps.

extraction.body: Apple announced an all-new MacBook Pro laptop with an OLED touchscreen at its “Pro and tell” event on Wednesday. It starts at $2,899 for the 14-inch model, or $3,399 for the 16-inch version, and it’s available to preorder today ahead of its release on November 6th. The new MacBook Pro has what Apple calls a “PROLED XDR” display, which is a tandem OLED screen. It’s equipped with M5 Pro or M5 Max chips — not the M6 chip on the other MacBook Pros announced this week. As for why you’d want to use the touchscreen, in addition to tasks like scrolling a webpage or zooming in on a photo, Apple offers examples like testing iOS and iPadOS apps directly on the display or playing software instruments on the screen. In a press release, Apple said its apps are optimized for touch and that an updated API will let developers add touch to their own apps. The 14-inch model weighs 3 pounds, and the 16-inch model weighs 4 pounds, according to Apple. Both laptops are also thinner; the 16-inch version is “nearly a millimeter” thinner, while the 14-inch one is half a millimeter thinner, Apple says. And Apple has bumped up the screen sizes by slimming down the bezels; the smaller model has a 14.2-inch screen size, while the bigger one is now 16.3 inches. The laptop offers “up to” 24 hours of battery life. The laptop supports three external displays simultaneously or four if you get an M5 Max version. extraction.body: The MacBook Pro has had pretty much the same design since 2021, but today at its 'Pro and Tell' event in Cupertino, Apple has announced an all-new MacBook Pro with a touchscreen. The new 'MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display' comes in either a 14- or 16-inch design, just like any other MacBook Pro, just with a Tandem OLED touch display with up to 128GB of RAM. But while the regular MacBook Pro 14 was updated with the M6 chip yesterday, this new touchscreen MacBook Pro will be equipped with either the M5 Pro or M5 Max, both of which will still be more powerful than Apple's new mainstream SoC. The display is the real star of the show, though, and it should be absolutely gorgeous, coming in with up to 2,000 nits of brightness and a color gamut that covers both the P3 and Adobe RGB spectrums. Couple that with the powerful chips, and this will likely be the laptop to beat for creative professionals who are comfortable on macOS. Touchscreen laptops have been around for a while, with Microsoft famously pushing for wide adoption of touch displays with Windows 8. At the time, though, Steve Jobs took a stand against touch displays, even claiming wholeheartedly that 'Touchscreen laptops don't work' back in 2010 . But even though Apple's dad wasn't a fan of touchscreens on laptops, this isn't the first time that Apple has had a touch display on a MacBook, at least if you count the controversial touch bar on the MacBook Pro in the late 2010s. However, it's clear that the RAM crisis has hit Apple as well. coreStoryFacts.text: Apple has officially announced the all-new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display, its first touchscreen laptop.
While Apple has innovated with multi-touch on the iPhone and iPad, the Mac has been resistant to touch input for years.
Back in March, Apple upgraded the standard 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro laptops to the current M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.
MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time, bringing pros a whole new way to interact with their content.
Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined.

Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place.
And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself.
Apple also touts the use of a new hinge technology in the MacBook Pro, in part to support touch input without compromising on stability:
The existing MacBook Pro configurations from March stick around at the same prices.
You just lose OLED, the glowing Apple logo, and the thinner and lighter design.
The new machines still use Touch ID with no Face ID support.
We’ll have to keep waiting for Face ID and built-in cellular connectivity.
Pre-orders are available starting today with deliveries starting November 6.
The new machine was first hinted at by Apple on October 19 with the company’s “Pro and tell” experience teaser .
Earlier today, new Apple CEO John Ternus shared a “spotlight” teaser for the laptop as well.
Apple’s Mac lineup consists of MacBook, MacBoo…
Touch also introduces entirely new ways of working for pro users.

In addition, a newly designed hinge provides greater stability while using Touch, and advanced video stabilization automatically smooths the camera feed in real time while using Touch on a video call.

As rumored, it includes an OLED display and, for the first time on macOS, a touchscreen—a change Apple has long debated. (Former CEO Steve Jobs famously was opposed.)

The OLED display (which Apple is, of course, calling the PROLED XDR) seems to be the real highlight here, compared to earlier models: It can achieve 2,000 nits in terms of maximum brightness, and Apple says it has a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.
References were made to burn-in protection, but details on which approach it’s taking for that weren’t yet shared.
The display retains the 120Hz variable refresh rate of its predecessors.
Memory configurations top out at the same places they did in the previous MacBook Pro models with M5 Max: up to 128 GB of RAM.
That said, storage can now go up to 16 TB—if you can afford it.
Beyond that, the design is largely similar to the existing one, but there are a few notable differences.
Apple said when announcing it that the 14-inch model is just 3 pounds, down around half a pound from the previous model, depending on configuration.

Apple’s demonstration video showed users interacting with applications by reaching up to touch the screen, including file dragging and multi-touch gestures like pinch-to-zoom.

Second, the top-of-screen camera notch has been replaced by the small black cutout that Apple calls the Dynamic Island.
Presumably it works similarly to the one we’ve seen on the iPhone, expanding or contracting to show live activities and other information.

passages: LOS ANGELES—Apple today announced and gave a first glimpse of its first major MacBook Pro redesign in more than five years.
As rumored, it includes an OLED display and, for the first time on macOS, a touchscreen—a change Apple has long debated. (Former CEO Steve Jobs famously was opposed.)

The OLED display (which Apple is, of course, calling the PROLED XDR) seems to be the real highlight here, compared to earlier models: It can achieve 2,000 nits in terms of maximum brightness, and Apple says it has a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.
References were made to burn-in protection, but details on which approach it’s taking for that weren’t yet shared.
The display retains the 120Hz variable refresh rate of its predecessors.
Memory configurations top out at the same places they did in the previous MacBook Pro models with M5 Max: up to 128 GB of RAM.
That said, storage can now go up to 16 TB—if you can afford it.
Beyond that, the design is largely similar to the existing one, but there are a few notable differences.
Apple said when announcing it that the 14-inch model is just 3 pounds, down around half a pound from the previous model, depending on configuration.
Ars Technica has been separating the signal from the noise for over 25 years.
With our unique combination of technical savvy and wide-ranging interest in the technological arts and sciences, Ars is the trusted source in a sea of information.
After all, you don’t need to know everything, only what’s important.
Apple’s demonstration video showed users interacting with applications by reaching up to touch the screen, including file dragging and multi-touch gestures like pinch-to-zoom.

The M6 series has already arrived in other Macs, but it seems Apple is skipping them for this refresh; there were previously reports that Apple planned to hold off on updating the chip until the M7 series, which could have significant improvements for AI performance, just like the recently released A20 Pro chip for the iPhone does.
Second, the top-of-screen camera notch has been replaced by the small black cutout that Apple calls the Dynamic Island.
Presumably it works similarly to the one we’ve seen on the iPhone, expanding or contracting to show live activities and other information.
Finally, there’s a retro throwback: The Apple logo on the back of the lid glows like the logo on MacBooks of yore.

extraction.body: Apple announced an all-new MacBook Pro laptop with an OLED touchscreen at its “Pro and tell” event on Wednesday. It starts at $2,899 for the 14-inch model, or $3,399 for the 16-inch version, and it’s available to preorder today ahead of its release on November 6th. The new MacBook Pro has what Apple calls a “PROLED XDR” display, which is a tandem OLED screen. It’s equipped with M5 Pro or M5 Max chips — not the M6 chip on the other MacBook Pros announced this week. As for why you’d want to use the touchscreen, in addition to tasks like scrolling a webpage or zooming in on a photo, Apple offers examples like testing iOS and iPadOS apps directly on the display or playing software instruments on the screen. In a press release, Apple said its apps are optimized for touch and that an updated API will let developers add touch to their own apps. The 14-inch model weighs 3 pounds, and the 16-inch model weighs 4 pounds, according to Apple. Both laptops are also thinner; the 16-inch version is “nearly a millimeter” thinner, while the 14-inch one is half a millimeter thinner, Apple says. And Apple has bumped up the screen sizes by slimming down the bezels; the smaller model has a 14.2-inch screen size, while the bigger one is now 16.3 inches. The laptop offers “up to” 24 hours of battery life. The laptop supports three external displays simultaneously or four if you get an M5 Max version. The new laptop follows what’s been a busy week of Apple announcements, including an iPad Mini with an OLED display and M6-powered iMacs.

sources.title: MacBook Pro With PROLED XDR Display Announced By Apple – The Company's First Touchscreen Laptop - IGN
passages: The new 'MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display' comes in either a 14- or 16-inch design, just like any other MacBook Pro, just with a Tandem OLED touch display with up to 128GB of RAM.

But while the regular MacBook Pro 14 was updated with the M6 chip yesterday, this new touchscreen MacBook Pro will be equipped with either the M5 Pro or M5 Max, both of which will still be more powerful than Apple's new mainstream SoC.
Touchscreen laptops have been around for a while, with Microsoft famously pushing for wide adoption of touch displays with Windows 8.
However, it's clear that the RAM crisis has hit Apple as well.
Of course, because it's a MacBook, you can absolutely max this thing out if you have the budget for it.
Though, that kind of configuration would be absolutely overkill unless you're editing 4K footage every day, and constantly leave your external drive at home.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen.
She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more.

extraction.body: The MacBook Pro has had pretty much the same design since 2021, but today at its 'Pro and Tell' event in Cupertino, Apple has announced an all-new MacBook Pro with a touchscreen. The new 'MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display' comes in either a 14- or 16-inch design, just like any other MacBook Pro, just with a Tandem OLED touch display with up to 128GB of RAM. But while the regular MacBook Pro 14 was updated with the M6 chip yesterday, this new touchscreen MacBook Pro will be equipped with either the M5 Pro or M5 Max, both of which will still be more powerful than Apple's new mainstream SoC. The display is the real star of the show, though, and it should be absolutely gorgeous, coming in with up to 2,000 nits of brightness and a color gamut that covers both the P3 and Adobe RGB spectrums. Couple that with the powerful chips, and this will likely be the laptop to beat for creative professionals who are comfortable on macOS. Touchscreen laptops have been around for a while, with Microsoft famously pushing for wide adoption of touch displays with Windows 8. At the time, though, Steve Jobs took a stand against touch displays, even claiming wholeheartedly that 'Touchscreen laptops don't work' back in 2010 . But even though Apple's dad wasn't a fan of touchscreens on laptops, this isn't the first time that Apple has had a touch display on a MacBook, at least if you count the controversial touch bar on the MacBook Pro in the late 2010s. However, it's clear that the RAM crisis has hit Apple as well. The new Touchscreen MacBook Pro costs an eye-watering $2,899 just to get in the door, which will get you the M5 Pro with a 15-core CPU and a 16-core GPU, along with 24GB of RAM and a 1TB SSD. The 16-inch model is even more expensive, and will set you back $3,399 to start, with a slightly more powerful M5 Pro configuration, along with the same 24GB RAM and 1TB SSD. Of course, because it's a MacBook, you can absolutely max this thing out if you have the budget for it. Apple will let you spec the 16-inch model with an M5 Max, with an 18-core CPU and 40-core GPU, along with 128GB of RAM and a 16TB SSD for $14,399. Though, that kind of configuration would be absolutely overkill unless you're editing 4K footage every day, and constantly leave your external drive at home. If you want to get your hands on the new MacBook Pro With PROLED XDR Display, you can preorder it today, and it will show up on store shelves on November 6. Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

sources.title: Apple launches new MacBook with touchscreen and OLED — starts at $2,899 - Tom's Hardware
passages: At an event in Los Angeles, the company detailed its new MacBook Pros featuring OLED XDR displays that you can control with your fingers.
The 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros are available for pre-order now and will ship on Nov.
The 14-incher will start at $2,899, while the 16-incher will start at $3,399.
The systems use Apple's existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and go up to 16TB of storage and 128GB of memory.
Apple's bezels are also less noticeable than before.
The hinge seems to be a point of pride (that's the second time this month, after the iPhone Duo).
In this case, it's that the screen is less prone to wobble when you touch it.
The new laptops are only slightly thinner than their predecessor.

Apple's own apps are already set to work with touch out of the box, and the company says many other apps will already work right away, including Notion, Canva, Zoom, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Adobe Lightroom, DaVinci Resolve, Blender, and more.
Apple already had the best speakers in a laptop, and now it's promising improvements: 50% deeper bass and new tweeters for clearer sound.
There's even dedicated audio tuning for people who want to use the spakers with their laptop lid closed.
The devices follow a long resistance to touchscreen laptops from Apple.
The iPad, too, has been vertical on Apple's keyboards, though some of those include touchpads as well).
The Mac resisted a touchscreen throughout former CEO Tim Cook's tenure, as well, though these new laptops definitely were developed under his leadership.

In the last decade, touchscreens have become a common feature on laptops running Windows, and Microsoft's latest operating system, Windows 11 , was designed to be slightly more touch-friendly than its predecessors.

A lover of all things gaming and tech, his previous work has shown up in Tom's Guide, Laptop Mag, Kotaku, PCMag and Complex, among others.

These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications. These systems also have light-up Apple logos, which we haven't seen on a MacBook Pro since 2016. The PROLED XDR display comes in 14.2 and 16.3-inch sizes, with ProMotion allowing for refresh rates between 10 Hz and 120 Hz. Apple claims 2,000 nits of peak brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio for intensely deep blacks. Apple's bezels are also less noticeable than before. The hinge seems to be a point of pride (that's the second time this month, after the iPhone Duo). In this case, it's that the screen is less prone to wobble when you touch it. The new laptops are only slightly thinner than their predecessor. There's even dedicated audio tuning for people who want to use the spakers with their laptop lid closed. The Mac resisted a touchscreen throughout former CEO Tim Cook's tenure, as well, though these new laptops definitely were developed under his leadership. extraction.body: Apple announced an all-new MacBook Pro laptop with an OLED touchscreen at its “Pro and tell” event on Wednesday. It starts at $2,899 for the 14-inch model, or $3,399 for the 16-inch version, and it’s available to preorder today ahead of its release on November 6th. The new MacBook Pro has what Apple calls a “PROLED XDR” display, which is a tandem OLED screen. It’s equipped with M5 Pro or M5 Max chips — not the M6 chip on the other MacBook Pros announced this week. As for why you’d want to use the touchscreen, in addition to tasks like scrolling a webpage or zooming in on a photo, Apple offers examples like testing iOS and iPadOS apps directly on the display or playing software instruments on the screen. In a press release, Apple said its apps are optimized for touch and that an updated API will let developers add touch to their own apps. The 14-inch model weighs 3 pounds, and the 16-inch model weighs 4 pounds, according to Apple. Both laptops are also thinner; the 16-inch version is “nearly a millimeter” thinner, while the 14-inch one is half a millimeter thinner, Apple says. And Apple has bumped up the screen sizes by slimming down the bezels; the smaller model has a 14.2-inch screen size, while the bigger one is now 16.3 inches. The laptop offers “up to” 24 hours of battery life. The laptop supports three external displays simultaneously or four if you get an M5 Max version. sources.title: Apple launches its new touchscreen MacBook Pro
passages: After years of resisting, Apple today launched a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen starting at $2,899.
The new Touchscreen MacBook marks two marquee product launches for new CEO John Turnus, who also introduced the company’s first foldable, the iPhone Duo, in September .
The new MacBook Pro more fully embraces the touchscreen, offering a new PROLED XDR Display in both 14-inch and 16-inch screen sizes.
The device is powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as options to choose from, along with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of storage.
The display has 2000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.
This also helps to stabilize the camera when you are on a video call and trying to access content on the display.

All of those new features and changes are enabled by a new screen technology that Apple calls PROLED XDR. That is Apple's branding for the OLED display that has featured on its iPads and iPhones, but never on a MacBook. They include redesigning the MacOS software so that users can more easily manipulate their content, as well as strengthening the hinge in the laptop so that it does not move when users are actually touching the screen. coreStoryFacts.text: At an event in Los Angeles, the company detailed its new MacBook Pros featuring OLED XDR displays that you can control with your fingers.
The 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros are available for pre-order now and will ship on Nov.
The 14-incher will start at $2,899, while the 16-incher will start at $3,399.

Apple's bezels are also less noticeable than before.
The hinge seems to be a point of pride (that's the second time this month, after the iPhone Duo).
In this case, it's that the screen is less prone to wobble when you touch it.
The new laptops are only slightly thinner than their predecessor.

Apple's own apps are already set to work with touch out of the box, and the company says many other apps will already work right away, including Notion, Canva, Zoom, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Adobe Lightroom, DaVinci Resolve, Blender, and more.
Apple already had the best speakers in a laptop, and now it's promising improvements: 50% deeper bass and new tweeters for clearer sound.
There's even dedicated audio tuning for people who want to use the spakers with their laptop lid closed.

That is compared with a starting price of $1,999 for the non-touchscreen version, though that also includes a less powerful chip.
The display allows for more vivid colours, blacker blacks and better contrast, Apple said.
All of those new features and changes are enabled by a new screen technology that Apple calls PROLED XDR.

Apple finally has touchscreen laptops. At an event in Los Angeles, the company detailed its new MacBook Pros featuring OLED XDR displays that you can control with your fingers. The 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros are available for pre-order now and will ship on Nov. 6. The 14-incher will start at $2,899, while the 16-incher will start at $3,399. The systems use Apple's existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and go up to 16TB of storage and 128GB of memory. These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch. These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications. These systems also have light-up Apple logos, which we haven't seen on a MacBook Pro since 2016. The PROLED XDR display comes in 14.2 and 16.3-inch sizes, with ProMotion allowing for refresh rates between 10 Hz and 120 Hz. Apple claims 2,000 nits of peak brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio for intensely deep blacks. These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch. These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications. The 14-inch MacBook Pro is 3 pounds, about half a pound less than the existing version, while the 16-inch MacBook Pro is 4 pounds, or 0.7 pounds lighter than it did before. Apple's bezels are also less noticeable than before. The hinge seems to be a point of pride (that's the second time this month, after the iPhone Duo). In this case, it's that the screen is less prone to wobble when you touch it. The new laptops are only slightly thinner than their predecessor. Apple claims that the 16-inch model is "nearly a millimeter thinner" and the 14-incher is "half a millimeter thinner." Apple attributes those shavings to OLED's display stack. Apple's own apps are already set to work with touch out of the box, and the company says many other apps will already work right away, including Notion, Canva, Zoom, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Adobe Lightroom, DaVinci Resolve, Blender, and more. Apple already had the best speakers in a laptop, and now it's promising improvements: 50% deeper bass and new tweeters for clearer sound. There's even dedicated audio tuning for people who want to use the spakers with their laptop lid closed. The significant change to the Mac is another in a flurry of launches for new CEO John Ternus, who also recently introduced the iPhone 18 Pro; the foldable iPhone Duo; Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4; HomeView; and a new iPad Mini, also with an OLED panel. The devices follow a long resistance to touchscreen laptops from Apple. Former CEO Steve Jobs, at an event introducing Mac OS X Lion in 2010, called laptops with touchscreens "ergonomically terrible" , claiming that "after an extended period of time, your arm wants to fall off." (HomeView, Apple's smart home manager, has a vertical touchscreen and no one has made a peep about that. The iPad, too, has been vertical on Apple's keyboards, though some of those include touchpads as well). The Mac resisted a touchscreen throughout former CEO Tim Cook's tenure, as well, though these new laptops definitely were developed under his leadership. In the last decade, touchscreens have become a common feature on laptops running Windows, and Microsoft's latest operating system, Windows 11 , was designed to be slightly more touch-friendly than its predecessors. Apple finally has touchscreen laptops. At an event in Los Angeles, the company detailed its new MacBook Pros featuring OLED XDR displays that you can control with your fingers. The 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros are available for pre-order now and will ship on Nov. 6. The 14-incher will start at $2,899, while the 16-incher will start at $3,399. The systems use Apple's existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and go up to 16TB of storage and 128GB of memory.

These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch. These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications. These systems also have light-up Apple logos, which we haven't seen on a MacBook Pro since 2016. The PROLED XDR display comes in 14.2 and 16.3-inch sizes, with ProMotion allowing for refresh rates between 10 Hz and 120 Hz. Apple claims 2,000 nits of peak brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio for intensely deep blacks.

These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch. These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications.

The 14-inch MacBook Pro is 3 pounds, about half a pound less than the existing version, while the 16-inch MacBook Pro is 4 pounds, or 0.7 pounds lighter than it did before. Apple's bezels are also less noticeable than before. The hinge seems to be a point of pride (that's the second time this month, after the iPhone Duo). In this case, it's that the screen is less prone to wobble when you touch it. The new laptops are only slightly thinner than their predecessor. Apple claims that the 16-inch model is "nearly a millimeter thinner" and the 14-incher is "half a millimeter thinner." Apple attributes those shavings to OLED's display stack. Apple's own apps are already set to work with touch out of the box, and the company says many other apps will already work right away, including Notion, Canva, Zoom, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Adobe Lightroom, DaVinci Resolve, Blender, and more. Apple already had the best speakers in a laptop, and now it's promising improvements: 50% deeper bass and new tweeters for clearer sound. There's even dedicated audio tuning for people who want to use the spakers with their laptop lid closed.

The significant change to the Mac is another in a flurry of launches for new CEO John Ternus, who also recently introduced the iPhone 18 Pro; the foldable iPhone Duo; Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4; HomeView; and a new iPad Mini, also with an OLED panel.

The devices follow a long resistance to touchscreen laptops from Apple. Former CEO Steve Jobs, at an event introducing Mac OS X Lion in 2010, called laptops with touchscreens "ergonomically terrible" , claiming that "after an extended period of time, your arm wants to fall off." (HomeView, Apple's smart home manager, has a vertical touchscreen and no one has made a peep about that. The iPad, too, has been vertical on Apple's keyboards, though some of those include touchpads as well). The Mac resisted a touchscreen throughout former CEO Tim Cook's tenure, as well, though these new laptops definitely were developed under his leadership. In the last decade, touchscreens have become a common feature on laptops running Windows, and Microsoft's latest operating system, Windows 11 , was designed to be slightly more touch-friendly than its predecessors. passages: On a 2012 earnings call, former CEO Tim Cook, responding to a question about why he doesn’t think the tablet and laptop will converge, said, “You can converge a toaster and a refrigerator, but those things are probably not going to be pleasing to the user.” In 2010, Steve Jobs called touchscreen laptops “ergonomically terrible.” Apple tried replacing the function keys with the Touch Bar on MacBook Pros starting in 2016, but it went back to physical function keys with the 2021 MacBook Pro redesign and fully dropped the Touch Bar in 2023.
Apple announced an all-new MacBook Pro laptop with an OLED touchscreen at its “Pro and tell” event on Wednesday.
The 14-inch model weighs 3 pounds, and the 16-inch model weighs 4 pounds, according to Apple.

Many of its executives, including new chief executive John Ternus, have previously dismissed the idea – primarily because of the ergonomic troubles of reaching out across the keyboard to touch the display. passages: By Dina Bass OpenAI intends to buy artificial intelligence computing chips from Alphabet Inc.’s Google, according to a person familiar with the matter, part of broader efforts by the ChatGPT maker to build out its AI infrastructure.
The Information previously reported that OpenAI was planning to buy Google chips.
OpenAI’s in-house Jalapeno chips, developed with Broadcom Inc., were created with help from Google veterans.
The company has already announced plans to start using its own chips to support its artificial intelligence models later this year.
Richard Ho, who runs the OpenAI internal chip team, was previously involved in the development of Google’s semiconductors — known as tensor processing units, or TPUs.

Oracle Corp. also announced on Tuesday that TPUs would be available through its cloud-computing infrastructure. “The next generation of AI will require a diverse range of compute,” Google executive Amin Vahdat said in a statement announcing that deal.
Google began working on its TPUs more than a decade ago.

Google Tensor Processing Units represent a formidable alternative. Originally designed for internal use, TPUs have evolved into highly efficient custom silicon optimized for machine learning workloads. Industry analysts note that TPUs are often more energy-efficient and potentially cheaper than comparable GPUs, particularly for inference tasks. Google expects TPU shipments to reach 4.3 million units in 2026, scaling significantly as the company pushes to expand its external cloud silicon business. The potential Google partnership is just one pillar of a broader infrastructure strategy. The company is simultaneously investing heavily in developing proprietary hardware. In June 2026, OpenAI and Broadcom unveiled their first custom AI chip, an inference processor designed specifically to improve performance and efficiency. The combination of purchasing Google TPUs, utilizing Nvidia GPUs, and deploying custom Broadcom-designed chips creates a highly diversified compute portfolio. These maneuvers mirror a wider shift across the technology sector. Major cloud providers and AI developers are no longer content to rely solely on merchant silicon. Amazon has aggressively expanded its Trainium and Inferentia chips, while Microsoft recently unveiled its custom Maia AI accelerator. As AI models grow larger and more complex, the cost of compute becomes a primary constraint on profitability and innovation. Securing alternative sources of processing power allows companies to negotiate better pricing, ensure supply continuity, and tailor hardware to specific software workloads. For Google, securing a major external customer would provide massive validation of its TPU architecture. The AI chip market is transitioning from a near-monopoly to a fragmented, multi-vendor ecosystem. While advanced architectures continue to set the benchmark for raw training performance, the rising importance of inference workloads is opening the door for specialized alternatives. Estimates suggest that inference could capture the larger share of AI compute demand as soon as 2027, a shift that heavily favors efficient architectures like TPUs and custom application-specific integrated circuits. Energy consumption is another critical factor driving the push for alternative silicon. Training and running massive language models requires gigawatts of data center capacity, straining local power grids and complicating corporate sustainability targets. Securing access to energy-efficient hardware allows developers to scale compute footprints without proportionally increasing carbon emissions. As the laboratory prepares for its next phase of growth, the ability to seamlessly orchestrate workloads across diverse silicon will be a critical competitive advantage. The outcome of current negotiations could reshape the economics of AI infrastructure, signaling the end of an era defined by single-vendor dependency.

coreStoryFacts.text: OpenAI (NASDAQ:OAI) is planning to purchase artificial intelligence chips developed by Alphabet's Google (NASDAQ:GOOG), according to a report published Tuesday by The Information, citing a person familiar with the matter.
The potential agreement would expand the commercial relationship between the two companies as demand for AI computing infrastructure continues to increase.
The reported plan to purchase Google-designed chips would extend the relationship into semiconductor procurement.
At the same time, Google Cloud provides computing infrastructure that can support the deployment of OpenAI models.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
Reuters reported in June 2025 that OpenAI had begun renting Google's AI chips, establishing an earlier commercial relationship involving the processors.
Despite that competition, the companies have increasingly established commercial arrangements involving computing infrastructure and AI services.
Alongside its reported interest in Google's chips, OpenAI is developing its own semiconductor technology.
Google did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment outside regular business hours, while OpenAI declined to comment.
The latest report suggests OpenAI is considering direct purchases rather than relying exclusively on rented computing capacity.
Developing proprietary processors could allow OpenAI to tailor hardware to its specific computing requirements while continuing to use chips supplied by external manufacturers.

The reported plans come as major technology companies commit substantial capital to data centres, processors and other infrastructure required to develop and operate advanced artificial intelligence models.
The agreement provides another distribution channel for OpenAI's advanced models while expanding the range of AI services available through Google's cloud platform.
Investors will examine the performance of Google Cloud and the company's spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure.
Google and OpenAI compete in areas including generative AI models, consumer applications and search-related services.
The developments highlight the increasing importance of semiconductor supply, computing costs and infrastructure investment as artificial intelligence companies expand their operations.
OpenAI said it planned to deploy the processor by the end of 2026 as part of a multigeneration chip development programme.

By Dina Bass OpenAI intends to buy artificial intelligence computing chips from Alphabet Inc.’s Google, according to a person familiar with the matter, part of broader efforts by the ChatGPT maker to build out its AI infrastructure.
The Information previously reported that OpenAI was planning to buy Google chips.
OpenAI’s in-house Jalapeno chips, developed with Broadcom Inc., were created with help from Google veterans.
The company has already announced plans to start using its own chips to support its artificial intelligence models later this year.
Richard Ho, who runs the OpenAI internal chip team, was previously involved in the development of Google’s semiconductors — known as tensor processing units, or TPUs.

Oracle Corp. also announced on Tuesday that TPUs would be available through its cloud-computing infrastructure. “The next generation of AI will require a diverse range of compute,” Google executive Amin Vahdat said in a statement announcing that deal.
Google began working on its TPUs more than a decade ago.

passages: By Dina Bass OpenAI intends to buy artificial intelligence computing chips from Alphabet Inc.’s Google, according to a person familiar with the matter, part of broader efforts by the ChatGPT maker to build out its AI infrastructure.
The Information previously reported that OpenAI was planning to buy Google chips.
OpenAI’s in-house Jalapeno chips, developed with Broadcom Inc., were created with help from Google veterans.
The company has already announced plans to start using its own chips to support its artificial intelligence models later this year.
Richard Ho, who runs the OpenAI internal chip team, was previously involved in the development of Google’s semiconductors — known as tensor processing units, or TPUs.

Oracle Corp. also announced on Tuesday that TPUs would be available through its cloud-computing infrastructure. “The next generation of AI will require a diverse range of compute,” Google executive Amin Vahdat said in a statement announcing that deal.
Google began working on its TPUs more than a decade ago.

Hyperscalers and leading AI laboratories are actively seeking alternatives to the dominant market position of Nvidia amid persistent hardware constraints and escalating global demand for AI infrastructure.
Both OpenAI and Google declined to comment on the specifics of the negotiations.

OpenAI is in active discussions to purchase artificial intelligence computing chips from Alphabet Inc., marking a significant strategic pivot as the ChatGPT maker seeks to diversify its hardware supply chain and reduce heavy reliance on Nvidia.
The potential Google partnership is just one pillar of a broader infrastructure strategy.
In June 2026, OpenAI and Broadcom unveiled their first custom AI chip, an inference processor designed specifically to improve performance and efficiency.
For years, the AI laboratory has depended heavily on Microsoft Azure and clusters of Nvidia graphics processing units to train and run sophisticated models.
Nvidia currently controls an estimated 80 per cent of the AI accelerator market by revenue, making its hardware the undisputed industry standard.
However, this reliance creates supply chain bottlenecks and limits negotiating leverage for companies consuming compute at an unprecedented scale.
The combination of purchasing Google TPUs, utilizing Nvidia GPUs, and deploying custom Broadcom-designed chips creates a highly diversified compute portfolio.
