The potential deal, first reported by The Information and subsequently confirmed by Bloomberg, reflects the multipronged approach of the AI laboratory to secure massive processing power. While final terms of any agreement remain undisclosed and discussions are private, the move signals a broader industry trend. Hyperscalers and leading AI laboratories are actively seeking alternatives to the dominant market position of Nvidia amid persistent hardware constraints and escalating global demand for AI infrastructure. Both OpenAI and Google declined to comment on the specifics of the negotiations. For years, the AI laboratory has depended heavily on Microsoft Azure and clusters of Nvidia graphics processing units to train and run sophisticated models. Nvidia currently controls an estimated 80 per cent of the AI accelerator market by revenue, making its hardware the undisputed industry standard. However, this reliance creates supply chain bottlenecks and limits negotiating leverage for companies consuming compute at an unprecedented scale. Google Tensor Processing Units represent a formidable alternative. Originally designed for internal use, TPUs have evolved into highly efficient custom silicon optimized for machine learning workloads. Industry analysts note that TPUs are often more energy-efficient and potentially cheaper than comparable GPUs, particularly for inference tasks. Google expects TPU shipments to reach 4.3 million units in 2026, scaling significantly as the company pushes to expand its external cloud silicon business. The potential Google partnership is just one pillar of a broader infrastructure strategy. The company is simultaneously investing heavily in developing proprietary hardware. In June 2026, OpenAI and Broadcom unveiled their first custom AI chip, an inference processor designed specifically to improve performance and efficiency. This collaboration with Broadcom is substantial. The chip design firm is reportedly arranging massive financing to support the production and deployment of these custom accelerators. By designing proprietary silicon, the AI developer aims to optimize hardware specifically for unique architectural needs, further insulating itself from the volatile merchant chip market. The combination of purchasing Google TPUs, utilizing Nvidia GPUs, and deploying custom Broadcom-designed chips creates a highly diversified compute portfolio. These maneuvers mirror a wider shift across the technology sector. Major cloud providers and AI developers are no longer content to rely solely on merchant silicon. Amazon has aggressively expanded its Trainium and Inferentia chips, while Microsoft recently unveiled its custom Maia AI accelerator. Meta also continues to scale its internal training and inference accelerator program. This diversification is driven by both economic necessity and strategic autonomy. As AI models grow larger and more complex, the cost of compute becomes a primary constraint on profitability and innovation. Securing alternative sources of processing power allows companies to negotiate better pricing, ensure supply continuity, and tailor hardware to specific software workloads. For Google, securing a major external customer would provide massive validation of its TPU architecture. The AI chip market is transitioning from a near-monopoly to a fragmented, multi-vendor ecosystem. While advanced architectures continue to set the benchmark for raw training performance, the rising importance of inference workloads is opening the door for specialized alternatives. Estimates suggest that inference could capture the larger share of AI compute demand as soon as 2027, a shift that heavily favors efficient architectures like TPUs and custom application-specific integrated circuits. Energy consumption is another critical factor driving the push for alternative silicon. Training and running massive language models requires gigawatts of data center capacity, straining local power grids and complicating corporate sustainability targets. Securing access to energy-efficient hardware allows developers to scale compute footprints without proportionally increasing carbon emissions. As the laboratory prepares for its next phase of growth, the ability to seamlessly orchestrate workloads across diverse silicon will be a critical competitive advantage. The outcome of current negotiations could reshape the economics of AI infrastructure, signaling the end of an era defined by single-vendor dependency.

sources.title: Meta's Waddle World Is A Tamagotchi-Like AI Pet App - Engadget
passages: Looks like a big part of Meta's AI strategy is to rely on "uwu" and cuteness as a way to get people to use and train its models and agents.
The company has released a new Tamagotchi-like AI-powered pet-rearing game called Waddle World , but it's only available in the Philippines for now.
If you've ever played Tamagotchi or any other virtual pet game , Waddle World will feel very familiar.
You hatch an egg to get a pet, then you have to play with it and feed it to keep you happy.
This virtual pet, however, can chat with you and even create illustrated journal entries to illustrate your conversations.
Social media consultant Matt Navarra has posted links to its Apple App Store and Google Play store listings on X.

sources.title: Meta has a new AI pet app called Waddle World
passages: Continuing its fast-paced experiments with AI apps, Meta has now launched a new app called Waddle World, which essentially looks like a Tamagotchi clone, but with AI.
It might be a test, but it could very well be a precursor to the company’s Tamagotchi-like gadget powered by Muse .
“Waddle World is a cozy 16-bit world where your pixel pet lives.
Hatch a virtual pet, visit whenever you like, and let it get to know you.
No pressure, no streaks to protect, no scores to chase — just a warm little escape in the cracks of your day,” the app’s description reads.
The company has launched Waddle World in the Philippines on both iOS and Android.
We have reached out to Meta for a comment on wider availability, and will update this piece if we hear back.
Meta may be wanting to stay away from building companion apps, given companies like Character.AI and OpenAI have faced lawsuits that allege their products caused harm to teenagers.

It might be a test, but it could very well be a precursor to the company’s Tamagotchi-like gadget powered by Muse . The company has launched Waddle World in the Philippines on both iOS and Android. The app, spotted by social media consultant Matt Navarra , lets you pick and grow a virtual pet, feed it, and play with it. We have reached out to Meta for a comment on wider availability, and will update this piece if we hear back. Meta’s description of the app indicates that it doesn’t want the app to be a habit builder. The company’s page also says that the app is not a chatbot, and is flagged as suitable for users older than 18. “Waddle World is a cozy 16-bit world where your pixel pet lives. Hatch a virtual pet, visit whenever you like, and let it get to know you. No pressure, no streaks to protect, no scores to chase — just a warm little escape in the cracks of your day,” the app’s description reads. “Not a chatbot. Not an assistant. Not a productivity tool. It’s a pet, and a place. Stay two minutes or twenty — it’ll be happy either way.” The app also doubles as a journal, letting users describe their day through voice or text. The pet listens to the user and writes up the note in its own voice as an entry with a doodle. The app also features mini-games that you can play over a few minutes, and can send you a weekly email based on what it learned about you. Meta may be wanting to stay away from building companion apps, given companies like Character.AI and OpenAI have faced lawsuits that allege their products caused harm to teenagers. Until now, the social media giant has released AI-centric apps like Pocket, which lets you vibe-code games , and Vibes, which lets you quickly generate videos . Besides virtual pets, some companies have also tried making hardware AI pets . sources.title: Meta's Waddle World is a Tamagotchi-style AI pet, now live in the Philippines - news.lavx.hu
passages: The pitch borrows straight from a 1996 handheld toy.
You hatch an egg, feed the creature, play with it, and keep it in a good mood.
Waddle World adds one twist to that loop: the pet talks back.
Meta describes the 16-bit game as a "daily journal disguised as a pet." You write or dictate an entry, the pet replies, and the app renders that reply as a doodle in your journal.
Meta's models generate both the response and the illustration.
Meta shipped a virtual pet game that runs on its own AI models, and right now you can only play it in the Philippines.
The app, called Waddle World , appeared on the Apple App Store and Google Play in late September, according to listings that social media consultant Matt Navarra posted on X .
Meta has not said when or whether Waddle World leaves the Philippines.
Watch the store listings and the Muse Charm's December launch for the answer.
Virtual pets lost their cultural moment decades ago, and reviving the form may say more about Meta's appetite for nostalgia than about what users want from AI.
The mini-games in Waddle World are competent and unremarkable.
If the pet's replies prove shallow after a week, the daily feeding loop turns into a chore, and a chore is exactly the thing that kills a Tamagotchi.
Cuteness also lowers the barrier for people who avoid chatbots.
Plenty of users find a text box intimidating and a pixel creature that wants breakfast approachable.
Meta's choice of the Philippines fits that logic.
The country has one of the world's most active social media populations, English runs through daily life, and mobile games already dominate leisure time.
A test market with dense usage and low acquisition cost tells Meta fast whether the retention curve holds.
Journaling apps collect the most sensitive material a person produces, and Waddle World wraps that material in a conversation with a character children understand as a friend.
The company has not published details on how journal text is stored, whether it trains future models, or how it handles entries from users under 13.
Those answers matter more for a diary than for a search query.
The app ships with a narrow test footprint and a familiar play loop that doubles as AI training.
Waddle World sits inside a broader Meta push to make its AI feel like a companion rather than a utility.
The company already lets you build a cartoon avatar and assign it a personality, an agent it calls Muse.
The Charm houses your Muse avatar in hardware, keeping the agent with you through the day.
Meta aims to release it in December, timed for the holidays.
The pattern across these products is engagement dressed as affection.
A chatbot you open on a desktop gets used when you remember it.
A pet that expects feeding every day trains a habit.
Every journal entry you write to Waddle World produces a paired dataset: your prompt, the model's response, and a signal that you came back to read it.
Games with collection mechanics and daily rewards are proven retention engines, and Meta gets conversational data at a scale surveys and lab tests cannot match.
Until Meta says otherwise, the Philippines-only footprint reads as an experiment with an uncertain destination.

Meta shipped a virtual pet game that runs on its own AI models, and right now you can only play it in the Philippines. The app, called Waddle World , appeared on the Apple App Store and Google Play in late September, according to listings that social media consultant Matt Navarra posted on X .

The pitch borrows straight from a 1996 handheld toy. You hatch an egg, feed the creature, play with it, and keep it in a good mood. Waddle World adds one twist to that loop: the pet talks back. Meta describes the 16-bit game as a "daily journal disguised as a pet." You write or dictate an entry, the pet replies, and the app renders that reply as a doodle in your journal. Meta's models generate both the response and the illustration.

Between diary sessions, you play mini-games to earn points toward food and toys. One has you stacking groceries on the pet's head. Another sends you catching falling stars while you dodge bombs. The third asks you to spell words from scrambled letters. Navarra summarized the whole concept as "Tamagotchi meets ChatGPT," and the description fits.

Waddle World sits inside a broader Meta push to make its AI feel like a companion rather than a utility. The company already lets you build a cartoon avatar and assign it a personality, an agent it calls Muse. At Meta Connect in September , the company revealed the Muse Charm, an egg-shaped device small enough to hang on a keychain. The Charm houses your Muse avatar in hardware, keeping the agent with you through the day. Meta aims to release it in December, timed for the holidays.

coreStoryFacts.text: Looks like a big part of Meta's AI strategy is to rely on "uwu" and cuteness as a way to get people to use and train its models and agents.
The company has released a new Tamagotchi-like AI-powered pet-rearing game called Waddle World , but it's only available in the Philippines for now.
If you've ever played Tamagotchi or any other virtual pet game , Waddle World will feel very familiar.
You hatch an egg to get a pet, then you have to play with it and feed it to keep you happy.
This virtual pet, however, can chat with you and even create illustrated journal entries to illustrate your conversations.
Social media consultant Matt Navarra has posted links to its Apple App Store and Google Play store listings on X.
Based on those listings, the game first became available in late September.
Every time you write in your diary, your pet writes back and draws a little doodle to go with the entry.
As Navarra noted, this is basically "Tamagotchi meets ChatGPT."
Meta already lets you design cute avatars and designate a personality for your Muse agent.
It also revealed the "Muse Charm" at its Connect event in September.
It's small enough to be a keychain, created so that you'll have constant access to Muse — or for Muse to have constant access to your environments and experiences.
Meta is aiming to release the device in time for the holidays this December.
Continuing its fast-paced experiments with AI apps, Meta has now launched a new app called Waddle World, which essentially looks like a Tamagotchi clone, but with AI.
It might be a test, but it could very well be a precursor to the company’s Tamagotchi-like gadget powered by Muse .
“Waddle World is a cozy 16-bit world where your pixel pet lives.
Hatch a virtual pet, visit whenever you like, and let it get to know you.
No pressure, no streaks to protect, no scores to chase — just a warm little escape in the cracks of your day,” the app’s description reads.
The company has launched Waddle World in the Philippines on both iOS and Android.
We have reached out to Meta for a comment on wider availability, and will update this piece if we hear back.
Meta may be wanting to stay away from building companion apps, given companies like Character.AI and OpenAI have faced lawsuits that allege their products caused harm to teenagers.

sources.title: Meta has a new AI pet app called Waddle World
passages: Continuing its fast-paced experiments with AI apps, Meta has now launched a new app called Waddle World, which essentially looks like a Tamagotchi clone, but with AI.
It might be a test, but it could very well be a precursor to the company’s Tamagotchi-like gadget powered by Muse .
“Waddle World is a cozy 16-bit world where your pixel pet lives.
Hatch a virtual pet, visit whenever you like, and let it get to know you.
No pressure, no streaks to protect, no scores to chase — just a warm little escape in the cracks of your day,” the app’s description reads.
The company has launched Waddle World in the Philippines on both iOS and Android.
We have reached out to Meta for a comment on wider availability, and will update this piece if we hear back.
Meta may be wanting to stay away from building companion apps, given companies like Character.AI and OpenAI have faced lawsuits that allege their products caused harm to teenagers.

It might be a test, but it could very well be a precursor to the company’s Tamagotchi-like gadget powered by Muse . The company has launched Waddle World in the Philippines on both iOS and Android. The app, spotted by social media consultant Matt Navarra , lets you pick and grow a virtual pet, feed it, and play with it. We have reached out to Meta for a comment on wider availability, and will update this piece if we hear back. Meta’s description of the app indicates that it doesn’t want the app to be a habit builder. The company’s page also says that the app is not a chatbot, and is flagged as suitable for users older than 18. “Waddle World is a cozy 16-bit world where your pixel pet lives. It’s a pet, and a place. Stay two minutes or twenty — it’ll be happy either way.” The app also doubles as a journal, letting users describe their day through voice or text. The pet listens to the user and writes up the note in its own voice as an entry with a doodle. The app also features mini-games that you can play over a few minutes, and can send you a weekly email based on what it learned about you. Meta may be wanting to stay away from building companion apps, given companies like Character.AI and OpenAI have faced lawsuits that allege their products caused harm to teenagers. Until now, the social media giant has released AI-centric apps like Pocket, which lets you vibe-code games , and Vibes, which lets you quickly generate videos . Besides virtual pets, some companies have also tried making hardware AI pets . extraction.body: Ahead of its 'Pro and Tell' event, the company has already launched a few new devices. Apple wasn't done with its product reveals for the fall after unveiling the iPhone Duo , iPhone 18 Pro models and an array of smart home devices . Nor could it wait until the third event of the season, dubbed "Pro and Tell," to show off more gear. The company got a string of announcements underway on Monday with the reveal of the long-awaited OLED iPad mini. Tuesday brought us an M6-powered iMac and 14-inch MacBook Pro. It's expected that Apple will unveil a touchscreen MacBook as well. Elsewhere, Apple released the latest versions of its operating systems. Among other things, those added more Siri AI features and made the assistant available in more languages. The company updated Apple Creator Studio with more AI features and creative tools as well. We'll update this story if and when Apple makes more announcements. In the meantime, here's everything Apple has announced so far this week. It feels like we've been waiting for forever for Apple to put an OLED display in the iPad mini but that day has finally arrived. The new display has double the peak brightness of the one on the previous model at 1,200 nits, and it has a 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio. The base storage remains the same at 128GB, though if you opt for 256GB or 512GB of storage, you can snag a variant with a nano-texture glass display. That'll cost you extra, naturally. The company managed to squeeze in a larger screen — an 8.5-inch display rather than the 8.3-inch one in the previous model — without increasing the size of the tablet. In fact, the new iPad mini is slightly narrower than the last one, at 5.22 inches vs. 5.3 inches. It's lighter as well, with the Wi-Fi model coming in at 0.56 pounds (compared with 0.65 pounds last time) and the 5G variant weighing 0.58 pounds (versus 0.66 pounds). The latter, by the way, now boasts Apple's C2 modem, which is said to deliver up to 50 percent faster data speeds than the previous iPad mini. There's also Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread connectivity thanks to the N1 chip. The OLED iPad mini — the eighth generation of the device — runs on the A20 Pro, the same chipset as the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo. Apple says the SoC is capable of running large language models locally, in case you're into that kind of thing. Otherwise, the tablet should be notably faster than earlier models. It supports Apple Intelligence and Siri AI as well, of course. The chipset also boasts a 7-core GPU — two more cores than the A17 Pro, which powered the last-gen iPad mini. On the camera front, there's a 12MP Center Stage lens on front of the tablet, which Apple has finally shifted to the landscape edge on the iPad mini. However, there's still no Face ID. The 12MP camera on the rear supports 4K 60fps video capture and Smart HDR 4. The 8th-gen iPad mini has a sealed enclosure to help protect it from the elements. The tablet has an IP67 rating, meaning that it should withstand dust and being immersed in a meter of freshwater for up to 30 minutes, though I would advise against intentionally submerging your iPad mini. As for battery life, Apple says that should be roughly the same as last time. The company says the new iPad mini should run for up to 10 hours when you're watching video or surfing the web over Wi-Fi. That drops down to nine hours if you're browsing over a cellular connection. If you have at least a 35W power adaptor, you'll be able to recharge the battery to 50 percent of its capacity in 30 minutes, Apple says. The most interesting thing to me about this iPad mini is that it has Apple's first Acoustic Display, which the company says helps it deliver "an even better audio experience." It claims the tablet offers more volume and "punchier bass" thanks to woofers that "are paired through the display." Apple added that "custom tweeters are now hidden between the glass and aluminum enclosure for clearer highs." I'm definitely curious to find out how all of that sounds in practice. Inevitably, the latest iPad mini comes with a price hike. It starts at $699, which is $150 more than the previous model after Apple increased the price of that in June . Pre-orders open on October 28, and the tablet will hit shelves on November 6. On Tuesday, Apple gave the iMac and MacBook Pro spec bumps. The desktop and laptop now each have the M6 chipset , which recently debuted in the Mac mini . Let's start with the new iMac . Apple says the M6's dual 16-core neural engine enables it to deliver up to five times faster on-device AI performance (for Siri AI, Apple Intelligence and local LLMs) than the previous-gen iMac from 2024 , which had the M4 chipset. The M6 is said to deliver up to 1.5 times faster performance than the M4 for daily tasks, up to two times faster graphics performance (for photo editing etc.) and up to two times higher gaming performance with ray tracing. The base-level M6 has 10 CPU cores (two super, three performance and two efficiency cores) and a 10-core CPU, compared with eight of each in the M4. There's the option to have a 12-core M6, in which case your desktop will have four Thunderbolt 4 ports instead of the two that the base model has. The four-port model has a nano-texture glass option as well. Elsewhere, Apple has introduced its N1 networking chip to the iMac. As such, the computer has support for Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread connectivity. It also has the option to add a 2.5Gb Ethernet port, an upgrade from gigabit Ethernet on the M4 iMac. Specs otherwise are the same as last time. You'll still get a 24-inch 4.5K Super Retina display, a 12MP Center Stage camera, a six‑speaker Dolby Atmos system, at least 16GB of RAM and 256GB of base storage. The dimensions are identical too, though the M6 iMac is a touch lighter than the previous gen at 9.7 pounds (versus 9.74 pounds). Don't expect any changes to the color options either — the new iMac is still available in blue, green, pink, yellow, purple, orange and silver. One other thing that's staying the same? The starting price, at least after the $200 increase that Apple gave the M4 iMac over the summer. The new model starts at $1,499, and the four-port version will run you at least $1,699. Pre-orders open October 28 and you'll be able to pick one up in store on November 6. The latest 14-inch MacBook Pro has the 12-core version of the M6 chipset and the N1 networking chip for Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread support. Those appear to be the only spec changes this time. Compared with the previous-gen 14-inch MBP, which had an M5 SoC, Apple says the M6 model offers up to 30 percent faster graphics performance and up to 25 percent faster AI workloads. It's said to deliver up to 1.3 faster rendering performance with ray tracing in Blender, up to 1.2 times faster image-processing performance in Affinity and up to 1.3 faster project build performance for compiling code in Xcode. It doesn't seem like this will be a massive upgrade for folks with an M5 model. However, if you have an older MacBook Pro (or really need those incremental improvements from the previous gen), it might be worth making the switch. Either way, creatives might want to take note of all the updates that are rolling out for Apple Creative Studio . Apple has given Final Cut Pro a long-awaited quality-of-life upgrade by letting you pull clips from the primary storyline and place them anywhere on the timeline, which seems like very basic functionality to have! MotionVFX is integrated into the app on Mac as well, so you'll have thousands of elements at your fingertips for your video edits. If you have a Mac that supports Apple Intelligence and is set to US English, Logic Pro has an "intelligent assistant" powered by OpenAI that's available in beta. The app has an an enhanced Stem Splitter that can now separate drums as well. In addition, Keynote, Pages and Numbers now have a chatbot you can use to adjust presentations, documents and spreadsheets. You won't have to pay more than you would have for the M5 model following this summer's price increase . The M6-powered 14-inch MacBook Pro starts at $1,999 for 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage. Again, pre-orders start on Wednesday with general availability to follow on November 6.

extraction.body: Ahead of its 'Pro and Tell' event, the company has already launched a few new devices. Apple wasn't done with its product reveals for the fall after unveiling the iPhone Duo , iPhone 18 Pro models and an array of smart home devices . Nor could it wait until the third event of the season, dubbed "Pro and Tell," to show off more gear. The company got a string of announcements underway on Monday with the reveal of the long-awaited OLED iPad mini. Tuesday brought us an M6-powered iMac and 14-inch MacBook Pro. It's expected that Apple will unveil a touchscreen MacBook as well. Elsewhere, Apple released the latest versions of its operating systems. Among other things, those added more Siri AI features and made the assistant available in more languages. The company updated Apple Creator Studio with more AI features and creative tools as well. We'll update this story if and when Apple makes more announcements. In the meantime, here's everything Apple has announced so far this week. It feels like we've been waiting for forever for Apple to put an OLED display in the iPad mini but that day has finally arrived. The new display has double the peak brightness of the one on the previous model at 1,200 nits, and it has a 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio. The base storage remains the same at 128GB, though if you opt for 256GB or 512GB of storage, you can snag a variant with a nano-texture glass display. That'll cost you extra, naturally. The company managed to squeeze in a larger screen — an 8.5-inch display rather than the 8.3-inch one in the previous model — without increasing the size of the tablet. In fact, the new iPad mini is slightly narrower than the last one, at 5.22 inches vs. 5.3 inches. It's lighter as well, with the Wi-Fi model coming in at 0.56 pounds (compared with 0.65 pounds last time) and the 5G variant weighing 0.58 pounds (versus 0.66 pounds). The latter, by the way, now boasts Apple's C2 modem, which is said to deliver up to 50 percent faster data speeds than the previous iPad mini. There's also Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread connectivity thanks to the N1 chip. The OLED iPad mini — the eighth generation of the device — runs on the A20 Pro, the same chipset as the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo. Apple says the SoC is capable of running large language models locally, in case you're into that kind of thing. Otherwise, the tablet should be notably faster than earlier models. It supports Apple Intelligence and Siri AI as well, of course. The chipset also boasts a 7-core GPU — two more cores than the A17 Pro, which powered the last-gen iPad mini. On the camera front, there's a 12MP Center Stage lens on front of the tablet, which Apple has finally shifted to the landscape edge on the iPad mini. However, there's still no Face ID. The 12MP camera on the rear supports 4K 60fps video capture and Smart HDR 4. The 8th-gen iPad mini has a sealed enclosure to help protect it from the elements. The tablet has an IP67 rating, meaning that it should withstand dust and being immersed in a meter of freshwater for up to 30 minutes, though I would advise against intentionally submerging your iPad mini. As for battery life, Apple says that should be roughly the same as last time. The company says the new iPad mini should run for up to 10 hours when you're watching video or surfing the web over Wi-Fi. That drops down to nine hours if you're browsing over a cellular connection. If you have at least a 35W power adaptor, you'll be able to recharge the battery to 50 percent of its capacity in 30 minutes, Apple says. The most interesting thing to me about this iPad mini is that it has Apple's first Acoustic Display, which the company says helps it deliver "an even better audio experience." It claims the tablet offers more volume and "punchier bass" thanks to woofers that "are paired through the display." Apple added that "custom tweeters are now hidden between the glass and aluminum enclosure for clearer highs." I'm definitely curious to find out how all of that sounds in practice. Inevitably, the latest iPad mini comes with a price hike. It starts at $699, which is $150 more than the previous model after Apple increased the price of that in June . Pre-orders open on October 28, and the tablet will hit shelves on November 6. On Tuesday, Apple gave the iMac and MacBook Pro spec bumps. The desktop and laptop now each have the M6 chipset , which recently debuted in the Mac mini . Let's start with the new iMac . Apple says the M6's dual 16-core neural engine enables it to deliver up to five times faster on-device AI performance (for Siri AI, Apple Intelligence and local LLMs) than the previous-gen iMac from 2024 , which had the M4 chipset. The M6 is said to deliver up to 1.5 times faster performance than the M4 for daily tasks, up to two times faster graphics performance (for photo editing etc.) and up to two times higher gaming performance with ray tracing. The base-level M6 has 10 CPU cores (two super, three performance and two efficiency cores) and a 10-core CPU, compared with eight of each in the M4. There's the option to have a 12-core M6, in which case your desktop will have four Thunderbolt 4 ports instead of the two that the base model has. The four-port model has a nano-texture glass option as well. Elsewhere, Apple has introduced its N1 networking chip to the iMac. As such, the computer has support for Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread connectivity. It also has the option to add a 2.5Gb Ethernet port, an upgrade from gigabit Ethernet on the M4 iMac. Specs otherwise are the same as last time. You'll still get a 24-inch 4.5K Super Retina display, a 12MP Center Stage camera, a six‑speaker Dolby Atmos system, at least 16GB of RAM and 256GB of base storage. The dimensions are identical too, though the M6 iMac is a touch lighter than the previous gen at 9.7 pounds (versus 9.74 pounds). Don't expect any changes to the color options either — the new iMac is still available in blue, green, pink, yellow, purple, orange and silver. One other thing that's staying the same? The starting price, at least after the $200 increase that Apple gave the M4 iMac over the summer. The new model starts at $1,499, and the four-port version will run you at least $1,699. Pre-orders open October 28 and you'll be able to pick one up in store on November 6. The latest 14-inch MacBook Pro has the 12-core version of the M6 chipset and the N1 networking chip for Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread support. Those appear to be the only spec changes this time. Compared with the previous-gen 14-inch MBP, which had an M5 SoC, Apple says the M6 model offers up to 30 percent faster graphics performance and up to 25 percent faster AI workloads. It's said to deliver up to 1.3 faster rendering performance with ray tracing in Blender, up to 1.2 times faster image-processing performance in Affinity and up to 1.3 faster project build performance for compiling code in Xcode. It doesn't seem like this will be a massive upgrade for folks with an M5 model. However, if you have an older MacBook Pro (or really need those incremental improvements from the previous gen), it might be worth making the switch. Either way, creatives might want to take note of all the updates that are rolling out for Apple Creative Studio . Apple has given Final Cut Pro a long-awaited quality-of-life upgrade by letting you pull clips from the primary storyline and place them anywhere on the timeline, which seems like very basic functionality to have! MotionVFX is integrated into the app on Mac as well, so you'll have thousands of elements at your fingertips for your video edits. If you have a Mac that supports Apple Intelligence and is set to US English, Logic Pro has an "intelligent assistant" powered by OpenAI that's available in beta. The app has an an enhanced Stem Splitter that can now separate drums as well. In addition, Keynote, Pages and Numbers now have a chatbot you can use to adjust presentations, documents and spreadsheets. You won't have to pay more than you would have for the M5 model following this summer's price increase . The M6-powered 14-inch MacBook Pro starts at $1,999 for 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage. Again, pre-orders start on Wednesday with general availability to follow on November 6.

Though Apple may have saved its biggest and most exciting update for last, it revealed a few other device upgrades and updates in the days leading up to its big reveal.
The company says the touch sensor is “built directly into the display panel,” not on top of it, which helps to reduce latency.
It’s also lighter than previous MacBook Pro models, with the 14-inch model weighing three pounds.
The device brings back the illuminated Apple logo on its lid as well, and is the first to come with a Dynamic Island for viewing real-time updates, searching for files, and using Siri AI.
The MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display starts at $2,899 with a 14-inch display and M5 Pro chip, while the 16-inch version starts at $3,399 with an M5 Pro.
The device is just 5.4mm thick, with bezels that are 24 percent slimmer than the previous generation.
It also comes with a new “Acoustic Display”, which Apple says includes woofers paired through the display for better bass and more volume.
Along with these updates, the iPad Mini also comes with Apple’s more powerful A20 Pro chip, a 12-megapixel camera in landscape orientation, and an IP67 rating for protection against water and dust.
Similar to its predecessor, the M6 MacBook Pro also offers a Liquid Retina XDR display with a nano-texture option, as well as a 12MP Center Stage camera.
You can preorder the new MacBook Pro today, which starts at $1,999 with a 12-core CPU, 12-core GPU, 16GB of memory, and 1TB of storage.
It also sports Apple’s new N1 wireless networking chip.

The chatbot is built using models from Apple and OpenAI, allowing it to do things like design and animate slides in Keynote; create and restructure drafts in Pages; and calculate and visualize data in Numbers.

extraction.body: The Trump administration is giving Constellation Energy $5 billion in loans to expand nuclear generating capacity at eight power plants by 1.1 gigawatts. Most or all of the additional power from seven of those facilities has already been bought by Google, Meta, or Amazon. Constellation said it plans to use the financing to “uprate” 11 existing reactors, an industry term for expanding capacity at a reactor, often by using more highly enriched uranium and by upgrading equipment to handle the increased power levels. The energy company said it had already committed to spending more than $7 billion to add 1,080 megawatts of nuclear capacity to deliver power to Google, Amazon, and Meta. The loan commitment, which has yet to be finalized, “could lower financing costs” for the projects, Constellation said in a press release . The eight power plants include six in Illinois (Braidwood, Byron, Clinton, Dresden, LaSalle, and Quad Cities), one in Maryland (Calvert Cliffs), and one in Pennsylvania (Limerick). Google is already the confirmed buyer of additional power from the Pennsylvania plant and four Illinois power plants, while Amazon is buying electricity from the Maryland plant and Meta is effectively buying the entire Clinton power plant in Illinois. On Tuesday, the Department of Energy touted the loan as supporting “affordable, reliable power to American homes and businesses,” though there is no evidence that the new nuclear capacity will lower prices for residential ratepayers. Constellation’s announcement does not say whether the projects will maintain or lower electricity rates, and the company would not confirm the government’s claim to TechCrunch. Hyperscalers, including Google, Amazon, and Meta, have been scouring the grid for additional capacity to support their AI data centers. Tech companies are paying handsomely for energy, committing tens of billions of dollars over the coming years. Given that power has become a competitive advantage, that estimate is probably on the low end. By lowering the cost of capital for the upgrades, the Department of Energy’s loans could boost Constellation’s bottom line, that of the hyperscalers — or both. Tim De Chant is a senior climate reporter at TechCrunch. He has written for a wide range of publications, including Wired magazine, the Chicago Tribune, Ars Technica, The Wire China, and NOVA Next, where he was founding editor. De Chant is also a lecturer in MIT’s Graduate Program in Science Writing, and he was awarded a Knight Science Journalism Fellowship at MIT in 2018, during which time he studied climate technologies and explored new business models for journalism. He received his PhD in environmental science, policy, and management from the University of California, Berkeley, and his BA degree in environmental studies, English, and biology from St. Olaf College. Department of Energy’s Office of Energy Dominance Financing to support nuclear uprates across select Constellation facilities. The potential funding would help accelerate projects that produce more reliable, around-the-clock power from existing nuclear plants to help meet growing energy demand. The DOE commitment builds on billions of dollars in private-sector investment already supporting Constellation’s efforts to increase nuclear output. An agreement announced last year with Meta also supports a 30-megawatt expansion at Clinton Clean Energy Center in Illinois . The conditional loan commitment could lower financing costs and help Constellation deliver additional nuclear capacity at greater scale. Uprates increase electricity production from existing plants, making them one of the fastest and most cost-effective ways to add dependable power without building entirely new generation facilities or transmission corridors. “This is how America wins the race for energy abundance – by pairing private-sector demand and investment with smart federal financing to unlock more power from the nuclear plants we already have,” said Joe Dominguez , Constellation chairman, president and CEO. “Our agreements with Google and Amazon demonstrate how long-term customer commitments can incentivize billions of dollars in investment in new, reliable nuclear capacity. This conditional loan commitment can help us move faster and go further, putting more reliable power on the grid, creating and preserving good-paying jobs, strengthening American energy security and helping families and businesses manage energy costs.” “The Energy Department is accelerating President Trump’s American nuclear renaissance and unlocking the full potential of our nation’s nuclear fleet,” said U.S . Secretary of Energy Chris Wright . “Uprates that maximize power generation from our existing nuclear facilities are yet another example of the commonsense energy addition policies the Trump Administration is embracing—ensuring more affordable, reliable, and secure energy for American families and businesses.” The potential investment advances the federal government’s effort to restore American nuclear leadership and reflects the goal of DOE’s UPRISE program: bringing the public and private sectors together to maximize electricity production from America’s existing nuclear fleet. The conditional commitment is subject to the completion of due diligence, negotiation of definitive financing documents and satisfaction of applicable conditions. It does not, by itself, represent a final Constellation decision to proceed with any individual uprate or at every facility under consideration. If finalized, Constellation will continue working with DOE, customers, regulators and local stakeholders to advance individual projects. We are also the largest nuclear energy company in the U.S. and a leading competitive retail supplier, serving approximately 2.5 million customer accounts nationwide, including 80% of the Fortune 100. Together, these agreements demonstrate how large energy users can help enable new, reliable generation that flows to the regional grid and benefits all customers.

The conditional loan commitment could lower financing costs and help Constellation deliver additional nuclear capacity at greater scale. Uprates increase electricity production from existing plants, making them one of the fastest and most cost-effective ways to add dependable power without building entirely new generation facilities or transmission corridors.

“This is how America wins the race for energy abundance – by pairing private-sector demand and investment with smart federal financing to unlock more power from the nuclear plants we already have,” said Joe Dominguez , Constellation chairman, president and CEO. “Our agreements with Google and Amazon demonstrate how long-term customer commitments can incentivize billions of dollars in investment in new, reliable nuclear capacity. This conditional loan commitment can help us move faster and go further, putting more reliable power on the grid, creating and preserving good-paying jobs, strengthening American energy security and helping families and businesses manage energy costs.”

“The Energy Department is accelerating President Trump’s American nuclear renaissance and unlocking the full potential of our nation’s nuclear fleet,” said U.S . Secretary of Energy Chris Wright . “Uprates that maximize power generation from our existing nuclear facilities are yet another example of the commonsense energy addition policies the Trump Administration is embracing—ensuring more affordable, reliable, and secure energy for American families and businesses.”

The potential investment advances the federal government’s effort to restore American nuclear leadership and reflects the goal of DOE’s UPRISE program: bringing the public and private sectors together to maximize electricity production from America’s existing nuclear fleet.

The conditional commitment is subject to the completion of due diligence, negotiation of definitive financing documents and satisfaction of applicable conditions. It does not, by itself, represent a final Constellation decision to proceed with any individual uprate or at every facility under consideration. extraction.body: Westinghouse AP-1000 nuclear reactor design has been a U.S. standard for decades, but more advanced technologies are also under development as sector sees Trump-led funding push and market resurgence. With surges in artificial intelligence and industrial manufacturing pushing utilities to keep up with record power demand, U.S. federal and state governments are expanding how nuclear power can fit into the energy mix—financing rapidly advancing technologies and offering incentives to speed development and reduce investment risk. Continuing its crusade to build out America's AI dominance, the Trump administration said June 23 it will offer loans totaling up to $17.5 billion to utilities and other energy companies to support development of 10 nuclear reactors at five sites. The U.S. Energy Dept. said it will make up to five loans, focused on the AP1000 design that has long been the U.S. standard for large commercial reactors. The agency said Westinghouse and a utility or company partner will jointly own each project and have to fully commit their project equity—$1-billion total per 1.1-GW project—upfront to access loan funds. DOE also said that the company, which manufactures the AP1000 design, will partner with up to five eligible U.S. utilities and energy firms to procure long-lead component items “at a fixed price.” According to the agency, the loans for bulk equipment purchases will boost the nuclear sector's efforts to restart and build new plants with needed financing, create new supply chain efficiencies and shorten project deployment timelines by up to three years. The last two U.S. nuclear units using the AP1000 design were completed in 2023 at Georgia Vogtle power plant, but the project was challenged with planning, supply chain, global pandemic and other issues, said Energy Secretary Chris Wright, He said the AP1000 design is "robust and sound," and worth replicating. “It’s another reason we’re working on building 10 plants,” he said, referencing the overall administration goal. “Think of the supply chain for that, and the same team can build in volume and at multiple locations." Wright claimed that the more standardized approach "will build a lot of construction expertise," adding that new plant cost and timing "will outperform what was done on Vogtle.” Looking for quick answers on construction and engineering topics? Try Ask ENR, our new smart AI search tool. Ask ENR → Purchases for each project “will be staggered based on the timing of equity commitments and other relevant factors,” according to the announcement. Westinghouse has signed letters of intent with seven potential partners, each with identified project sites, but not disclosed publicly. "The US has taken the biggest step towards a nuclear renaissance in decades," said Thomas Hochman, energy director at the Foundation for American Innovation, in a social media post. According to Washington, D.C.-based market research firm Capstone, the regulated utilities best positioned to access the DOE loans include Dominion Energy, DTE Energy, WEC Energy Group, Public Service Enterprise Group and Entergy Corp. It expects more details on loan recipients will be known by the end of the year. Loans would help companies procure items such as reactor vessels and steam generators, which can take years. "Long lead items funded by these loans are completely standardized to the point of being interchangeable between projects," Julie Kozeracki, acting chief investment officer in DOE's loan office, told media. The agency expects the program to expand U.S. nuclear plant manufacturing capacity, said Greg Beard, loan finance program chief. Some hyperscalers may even take equity stakes in nuclear plant projects, he added. "We are confident that these projects will be economic for utility shareholders, ratepayers and hyperscalers," Beard said, adding that a competitive process to select engineering, procurement and construction companies also is intended, but with no detail released. Wright said hyperscalers are expected to sign long-term offtake agreements up front for financial stability. Uncertainties over the loan program include how much funding DOE ultimately will cover for certain components, the utilities and companies to be involved, reactor locations and any impacts on planned construction starts. The announcement advances President Donald Trump's 2025 executive orders directing deployment of 300 GW of net new nuclear capacity by 2050 , and having 10 large reactors under construction by 2030. It also follows an $80-billion federal agreement with Westinghouse owners, Canada-based companies Cameco and Brookfield Asset Management, with which DOE would arrange financing and help secure reactor permits in exchange for a 20% share of future profits. The federal aim is to grow the U.S. nuclear footprint from about 100 GW to 400 GW by 2050. But concerns remain. Loans are “a drop in the bucket compared to the likely total project cost for ten AP1000 reactors,” Edwin Lyman, director of nuclear power safety at the Union of Concerned Scientists, told Utility Dive. The total cost could approach $200 billion, he said, adding that "none of these potential projects is backed up with an actual contract for construction.” He questioned if orders for components "will have to be cancelled if actual projects do not materialize.” Meanwhile more states are actively reconsidering new or expanded nuclear power. DOE claims more than 25 states have passed supportive legislation, which includes small modular reactors (SMRs) and other advanced next-generation technology. On June 24, Arizona Public Service, Salt River Project, and Tucson Electric Power announced they would add new generation to Palo Verde Generating Station, with some of its units in service for 40 years. Utilities said a siting study would finish in six months. Texas also wants more advanced nuclear, with the seeking applications for a $350-million nuclear construction fund . New York released this month a draft outline for its plan to develop 5 GW of new nuclear power across the state, including at least 1 GW upstate. According to the New York Power Authority, eight upstate communities and 23 developers have expressed interest in the effort, although a moratorium still exists in parts of the state, and legislators could weigh new proposed bans. New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill (D) signed legislation shortly after assuming office in January that removed a permitting hurdle which discouraged new nuclear capacity. "For costs to come down, we need more energy supply. New Jersey is well-positioned to be a leader in next-generation nuclear energy ... and we are open for business," she said. Two operating plants provide about 42% of the state's power. "We want 24/7 power. Where is the intersection between 24/7 power and the ability to scale?" Mike Kramer, Constellation's vice president for data economy strategy, told attedees at a Reuters energy conference in New York City June 23. "We won't see winners between renewables, nuclear and gas. There will be a lot of combination." Brian Savoy, CFO of Duke Energy, described as the largest regulated U.S. nuclear utility, noted that strong nuclear support from govenrments in countries such as Poland and China offer the "right amount of risk sharing." Meanwhile, a DOE pilot program to contract with 10 private firms to build and operate advanced experimental reactors outside of national laboratories is fast approaching a July 4 deadline to have at least three facilities reaching "nuclear criticality." With surges in artificial intelligence and industrial manufacturing pushing utilities to keep up with record power demand, U.S. federal and state governments are expanding how nuclear power can fit into the energy mix—financing rapidly advancing technologies and offering incentives to speed development and reduce investment risk.

The agency said Westinghouse and a utility or company partner will jointly own each project and have to fully commit their project equity—$1-billion total per 1.1-GW project—upfront to access loan funds.

“It’s another reason we’re working on building 10 plants,” he said, referencing the overall administration goal. “Think of the supply chain for that, and the same team can build in volume and at multiple locations." Purchases for each project “will be staggered based on the timing of equity commitments and other relevant factors,” according to the announcement. Westinghouse has signed letters of intent with seven potential partners, each with identified project sites, but not disclosed publicly. "The US has taken the biggest step towards a nuclear renaissance in decades," said Thomas Hochman, energy director at the Foundation for American Innovation, in a social media post.

According to Washington, D.C.-based market research firm Capstone, the regulated utilities best positioned to access the DOE loans include Dominion Energy, DTE Energy, WEC Energy Group, Public Service Enterprise Group and Entergy Corp. It expects more details on loan recipients will be known by the end of the year.

Loans would help companies procure items such as reactor vessels and steam generators, which can take years. "Long lead items funded by these loans are completely standardized to the point of being interchangeable between projects," Julie Kozeracki, acting chief investment officer in DOE's loan office, told media. The agency expects the program to expand U.S. nuclear plant manufacturing capacity, said Greg Beard, loan finance program chief. Some hyperscalers may even take equity stakes in nuclear plant projects, he added. Uncertainties over the loan program include how much funding DOE ultimately will cover for certain components, the utilities and companies to be involved, reactor locations and any impacts on planned construction starts.

relevantPassages.text: BALTIMORE --(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Constellation (Nasdaq: CEG ), the nation’s largest producer of reliable, emissions-free nuclear energy, today announced a conditional loan commitment of up to $5 billion from the U.S .
Department of Energy’s Office of Energy Dominance Financing to support nuclear uprates across select Constellation facilities.
The potential funding would help accelerate projects that produce more reliable, around-the-clock power from existing nuclear plants to help meet growing energy demand.
“Our agreements with Google and Amazon demonstrate how long-term customer commitments can incentivize billions of dollars in investment in new, reliable nuclear capacity.

Uprates increase electricity production from existing plants, making them one of the fastest and most cost-effective ways to add dependable power without building entirely new generation facilities or transmission corridors.
An agreement announced last year with Meta also supports a 30-megawatt expansion at Clinton Clean Energy Center in Illinois .
The conditional commitment is subject to the completion of due diligence, negotiation of definitive financing documents and satisfaction of applicable conditions.
It does not, by itself, represent a final Constellation decision to proceed with any individual uprate or at every facility under consideration.
If finalized, Constellation will continue working with DOE, customers, regulators and local stakeholders to advance individual projects.

“Uprates that maximize power generation from our existing nuclear facilities are yet another example of the commonsense energy addition policies the Trump Administration is embracing—ensuring more affordable, reliable, and secure energy for American families and businesses.”

extraction.body: Westinghouse AP-1000 nuclear reactor design has been a U.S. standard for decades, but more advanced technologies are also under development as sector sees Trump-led funding push and market resurgence. With surges in artificial intelligence and industrial manufacturing pushing utilities to keep up with record power demand, U.S. federal and state governments are expanding how nuclear power can fit into the energy mix—financing rapidly advancing technologies and offering incentives to speed development and reduce investment risk. Continuing its crusade to build out America's AI dominance, the Trump administration said June 23 it will offer loans totaling up to $17.5 billion to utilities and other energy companies to support development of 10 nuclear reactors at five sites. The U.S. Energy Dept. said it will make up to five loans, focused on the AP1000 design that has long been the U.S. standard for large commercial reactors. The agency said Westinghouse and a utility or company partner will jointly own each project and have to fully commit their project equity—$1-billion total per 1.1-GW project—upfront to access loan funds. DOE also said that the company, which manufactures the AP1000 design, will partner with up to five eligible U.S. utilities and energy firms to procure long-lead component items “at a fixed price.” According to the agency, the loans for bulk equipment purchases will boost the nuclear sector's efforts to restart and build new plants with needed financing, create new supply chain efficiencies and shorten project deployment timelines by up to three years. The last two U.S. nuclear units using the AP1000 design were completed in 2023 at Georgia Vogtle power plant, but the project was challenged with planning, supply chain, global pandemic and other issues, said Energy Secretary Chris Wright, He said the AP1000 design is "robust and sound," and worth replicating. “It’s another reason we’re working on building 10 plants,” he said, referencing the overall administration goal. “Think of the supply chain for that, and the same team can build in volume and at multiple locations." Wright claimed that the more standardized approach "will build a lot of construction expertise," adding that new plant cost and timing "will outperform what was done on Vogtle.” Looking for quick answers on construction and engineering topics? Ask ENR → Purchases for each project “will be staggered based on the timing of equity commitments and other relevant factors,” according to the announcement. Westinghouse has signed letters of intent with seven potential partners, each with identified project sites, but not disclosed publicly. "The US has taken the biggest step towards a nuclear renaissance in decades," said Thomas Hochman, energy director at the Foundation for American Innovation, in a social media post. According to Washington, D.C.-based market research firm Capstone, the regulated utilities best positioned to access the DOE loans include Dominion Energy, DTE Energy, WEC Energy Group, Public Service Enterprise Group and Entergy Corp. It expects more details on loan recipients will be known by the end of the year. Loans would help companies procure items such as reactor vessels and steam generators, which can take years. "Long lead items funded by these loans are completely standardized to the point of being interchangeable between projects," Julie Kozeracki, acting chief investment officer in DOE's loan office, told media. The agency expects the program to expand U.S. nuclear plant manufacturing capacity, said Greg Beard, loan finance program chief. Some hyperscalers may even take equity stakes in nuclear plant projects, he added. "We are confident that these projects will be economic for utility shareholders, ratepayers and hyperscalers," Beard said, adding that a competitive process to select engineering, procurement and construction companies also is intended, but with no detail released. Wright said hyperscalers are expected to sign long-term offtake agreements up front for financial stability. Uncertainties over the loan program include how much funding DOE ultimately will cover for certain components, the utilities and companies to be involved, reactor locations and any impacts on planned construction starts. The announcement advances President Donald Trump's 2025 executive orders directing deployment of 300 GW of net new nuclear capacity by 2050 , and having 10 large reactors under construction by 2030. It also follows an $80-billion federal agreement with Westinghouse owners, Canada-based companies Cameco and Brookfield Asset Management, with which DOE would arrange financing and help secure reactor permits in exchange for a 20% share of future profits. The federal aim is to grow the U.S. nuclear footprint from about 100 GW to 400 GW by 2050. But concerns remain. Loans are “a drop in the bucket compared to the likely total project cost for ten AP1000 reactors,” Edwin Lyman, director of nuclear power safety at the Union of Concerned Scientists, told Utility Dive. The total cost could approach $200 billion, he said, adding that "none of these potential projects is backed up with an actual contract for construction.” He questioned if orders for components "will have to be cancelled if actual projects do not materialize.” Meanwhile more states are actively reconsidering new or expanded nuclear power. DOE claims more than 25 states have passed supportive legislation, which includes small modular reactors (SMRs) and other advanced next-generation technology. On June 24, Arizona Public Service, Salt River Project, and Tucson Electric Power announced they would add new generation to Palo Verde Generating Station, with some of its units in service for 40 years. Utilities said a siting study would finish in six months. Texas also wants more advanced nuclear, with the seeking applications for a $350-million nuclear construction fund . New York released this month a draft outline for its plan to develop 5 GW of new nuclear power across the state, including at least 1 GW upstate. According to the New York Power Authority, eight upstate communities and 23 developers have expressed interest in the effort, although a moratorium still exists in parts of the state, and legislators could weigh new proposed bans. New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill (D) signed legislation shortly after assuming office in January that removed a permitting hurdle which discouraged new nuclear capacity. "For costs to come down, we need more energy supply. New Jersey is well-positioned to be a leader in next-generation nuclear energy ... and we are open for business," she said. Two operating plants provide about 42% of the state's power. "We want 24/7 power. Where is the intersection between 24/7 power and the ability to scale?" Mike Kramer, Constellation's vice president for data economy strategy, told attedees at a Reuters energy conference in New York City June 23. "We won't see winners between renewables, nuclear and gas. There will be a lot of combination." Brian Savoy, CFO of Duke Energy, described as the largest regulated U.S. nuclear utility, noted that strong nuclear support from govenrments in countries such as Poland and China offer the "right amount of risk sharing." Meanwhile, a DOE pilot program to contract with 10 private firms to build and operate advanced experimental reactors outside of national laboratories is fast approaching a July 4 deadline to have at least three facilities reaching "nuclear criticality." Two so far say they have passed that milestone—Antares Nuclear, a California microreactor developer, and Valar Atomics, now building an advanced reactor. “Two reactors have gone critical, for the first time in 40 years," Wright told Reuters attendees. "We expect the third by July 4," although he did not disclose the name of any firm set to do so. Also, despite federal support for the AP1000 nuclear design, AtkinsRéalis, developer of Canada’s core reactor design CANDU, which is cooled with pressurized heavy water, said June 24 that it has begun the process for U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission licensing. “As the United States enters a new chapter in its civilian nuclear program, AtkinsRealis is uniquely positioned, as the steward of CANDU technology, to help advance the country’s ambitious energy policy through proven, low-cost reactor technology with a world-class reputation,” said firm President and CEO Ian Edwards. Canada also has announced in recent days an updated national Nuclear Energy Strategy, a long-term vision of nuclear power potential that includes plans to deploy up to 10 new large-scale reactors by 2040 along with two ongoing projects in Ontario. The plan calls for at least one reactor outside Ontario to operate or be in construction by 2035, and a microreactor demonstrated by 2035 and deployed to a rural community by the late 2030s. The country would ensure that a "modernized, cost-competitive" CANDU reactor design is in place by 2030 for domestic use and potential export. "We are moving at speeds not seen in generations to get big things done and leveraging preexisting strengths to become a modern energy superpower," Minister of Energy and Natural Resources Tim Hodgson said in a statement. extraction.body: Apple on Tuesday unveiled its new 14-inch MacBook Pro, powered by its latest M6 chip. The new MacBook Pro has 24 hours of battery life and now supports Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 connectivity. The laptop starts at $1,999 and is available in space black and silver. Apple also announced its latest iMac , which is also powered by the M6 chip. The tech giant revealed the new devices just a day before its “Pro and Tell” event scheduled for Wednesday. On Monday, Apple announced its new iPad mini . The tech giant says the M6 chip features a 12-core CPU with the world’s fastest CPU core and a 12-core GPU that delivers more responsive performance, up to 30% faster graphics, and up to 25% faster AI workloads compared with the M5 chip. The M6 delivers up to 13 times the LLM prompt-processing speed of the M1 MacBook Pro and up to 1.3 times faster performance than the M5 model, Apple says. The M6 MacBook Pro starts with 16GB of unified memory, configurable up to 32GB, and has memory bandwidth of up to 170GB/s, up from the 153GB/s on the M5 chip. It includes HDMI, MagSafe 3, three Thunderbolt 4 ports, an SDXC card slot, and a headphone jack. Like previous models, the laptop features a 12-megapixel camera. The M6 MacBook Pro supports fast charging, reaching up to 50% charge in 30 minutes with a compatible high-wattage USB-C power adapter. As for the new M6-powered iMac, it features a faster CPU and GPU, with Neural Accelerators built into every core. Apple says the M6 delivers smooth multitasking and powerful performance for everyday apps, photo editing, and video production. The new iMac starts at $1,499 and comes in blue, green, pink, yellow, purple, orange, and silver. The company also notes that the new iMac delivers up to five times faster on-device AI performance than the M4 model. It features a 24-inch 4.5K Retina display, an advanced camera and audio system, up to four Thunderbolt 4 ports, color-matched accessories, and macOS 27. Both the new MacBook Pro and iMac can be preordered starting October 28 and will be available starting November 6. Aisha is a consumer news reporter at TechCrunch. Prior to joining the publication in 2021, she was a telecom reporter at MobileSyrup. The M6 MacBook Pro starts with 16GB of unified memory, configurable up to 32GB, and has memory bandwidth of up to 170GB/s, up from the 153GB/s on the M5 chip.
It includes HDMI, MagSafe 3, three Thunderbolt 4 ports, an SDXC card slot, and a headphone jack. Like previous models, the laptop features a 12-megapixel camera.
The M6 MacBook Pro supports fast charging, reaching up to 50% charge in 30 minutes with a compatible high-wattage USB-C power adapter.

As for the new M6-powered iMac, it features a faster CPU and GPU, with Neural Accelerators built into every core. Apple says the M6 delivers smooth multitasking and powerful performance for everyday apps, photo editing, and video production.
The new iMac starts at $1,499 and comes in blue, green, pink, yellow, purple, orange, and silver.

The company also notes that the new iMac delivers up to five times faster on-device AI performance than the M4 model. It features a 24-inch 4.5K Retina display, an advanced camera and audio system, up to four Thunderbolt 4 ports, color-matched accessories, and macOS 27.
Both the new MacBook Pro and iMac can be preordered starting October 28 and will be available starting November 6.

M6 features an advanced 12-core CPU with the world’s fastest CPU core, so everything from productivity tasks to more demanding pro workflows feels incredibly fast and responsive. 1 The 12-core GPU delivers up to 30 percent faster graphics and up to 25 percent faster AI workloads when compared to M5, making the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 a compelling value for users who need serious power. 2 For those upgrading from M1, the performance gains are even more significant, with up to 11x faster graphics and up to 13x faster AI performance. 3 With additional Neural Accelerators in the GPU and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, M6 turns MacBook Pro into an even more powerful platform for AI — from taking advantage of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features across apps and macOS to running LLMs locally, all while preserving user privacy. 4 In addition, the 14-inch MacBook Pro features Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, while superfast storage makes working with large files, exporting projects, and running demanding AI workflows fly. And with phenomenal battery life of up to 24 hours, it delivers the same remarkable performance whether plugged in or on battery, so users can work, create, and pursue their passions from anywhere. 3 It also offers the advanced features users love, including the stunning Liquid Retina XDR display with a nano-texture option, a 12MP Center Stage camera, an immersive six-speaker sound system, and a wide array of ports. Together with macOS 27, the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 is a major upgrade for existing Mac users and those coming to Mac for the first time. Available in space black and silver, it can be pre-ordered beginning tomorrow, October 28, with availability starting Friday, November 6.

“The 14-inch MacBook Pro is the pro laptop of choice for a wide range of users — from college students, to business professionals across every industry, to multidisciplinary creators doing it all on one device,” said Shelly Goldberg, Apple’s vice president of Hardware Engineering. “With the powerful M6 chip, we’re taking performance to the next level, with a boost in CPU speed and graphics and even more powerful capabilities for on-device AI. With its amazing battery life, remarkable Liquid Retina XDR display, and even faster connectivity, the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 delivers a fantastic combination of performance, capability, and value.”
M6: Blazing-Fast Performance and On-Device AI Capabilities

M6 brings even more performance and next-level AI capabilities to the 14-inch MacBook Pro. Featuring a powerful 12-core CPU, a 12-core GPU with Neural Accelerators in each core, Dual 16-core Neural Engine, and faster unified memory, MacBook Pro with M6 is faster and more responsive.

The 12-core CPU, with two more cores than before, brings blazing-fast single- and multithreaded performance, so users can fly through everything from multitasking across apps to compiling code to handling complex creative workflows. The 12-core GPU, also with two additional cores, delivers up to 30 percent faster graphics performance when compared to M5. 2 Everything from 3D modeling to photo editing and gaming feels incredibly fast, enhanced by a third-generation ray-tracing engine and Dynamic Caching to optimize on-chip memory. It also brings up to 25 percent faster performance for on-device AI workloads, like LLM prompt processing, compared to M5. 3 The Dual 16-core Neural Engine delivers up to 1.9x faster performance than M5 and works with the advanced GPU to dramatically accelerate AI workloads like image generation, Super Resolution, and AI upscaling. 2 The Neural Engine also powers Apple Intelligence, enabling advanced and energy-efficient on-device AI processing. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 does all this with industry-leading performance per watt and up to 24 hours of battery life, the longest ever in a Mac. With 16GB of unified memory standard, configurable up to 32GB, and higher memory bandwidth up to 170GB/s, MacBook Pro makes multitasking and working with demanding apps and large projects even faster.

There’s never been a better time for customers to upgrade from a previous-generation MacBook Pro with Apple silicon or an Intel-based Mac. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 delivers remarkable value thanks to major performance improvements and powerful AI capabilities. The new 14-inch MacBook Pro also features all of the compelling capabilities that have made it so popular, including:

The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 comes to life with macOS 27, which includes Siri AI, a profoundly more capable, conversational, and personal assistant; helpful Apple Intelligence features across everyday apps; and improvements that make the Mac even more responsive and reliable. Siri AI can draw on personal context to help users find what they need in the moment across messages, emails, photos, and more; answer questions about virtually any topic; and get things done across apps — all with groundbreaking privacy protections. Siri AI is integrated into Spotlight and systemwide context menus, and users can ask Siri about what’s on their display with Visual Intelligence using a dedicated keyboard shortcut. Users can also write and edit with Siri almost anywhere they type.

Additionally, Apple Intelligence makes apps smarter and more useful. In Safari, it powers new tools that automatically organize a user’s tabs into topics; notify them of website changes, like product restocks or price drops; and enable the creation of custom extensions based on a description. Users can also easily create an automation in Shortcuts by simply describing it, or tap into intelligent photo editing tools in the Photos app. The new 14-inch MacBook Pro gets even more responsive, reliable, and delightful with refinements to design, performance, search, and more. Updates to Liquid Glass deliver an even more focused and approachable experience. A new slider in Settings gives users the option to personalize Liquid Glass, adjusting it anywhere from ultraclear to fully tinted to match their preference, and app icons are sharper and more defined.
14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 and the Environment

The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030. It is made with 45 percent recycled content overall, 6 including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure, 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and, in a first for Apple, 100 percent recycled tantalum in multiple capacitors. It is manufactured with 60 percent renewable electricity, such as wind and solar, across the supply chain. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 is designed to be durable and repairable, and meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry. As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based 7 and designed to be recycled.

Apple revolutionized personal technology with the introduction of the Macintosh in 1984. Today, Apple leads the world in innovation with iPhone, iPad, Mac, AirPods, Apple Watch, and Apple Vision Pro. Apple’s six software platforms — iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, visionOS, and tvOS — provide seamless experiences across all Apple devices and empower people with breakthrough services including the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, iCloud, and Apple TV. Apple’s more than 150,000 employees are dedicated to making the best products on earth and to leaving the world better than we found it.
The latest news and updates, direct from Apple.

extraction.body: It's another big week for Apple, with a new iPad Mini, MacBook Pro and iMac, and more yet to come. Apple’s Pro and Tell experience week is here, and it’s off to a strong start, with the new iPad Mini unveiled on Monday morning and a new MacBook Pro and iMac on Tuesday. But there’s more to come: We’re also expecting a long-anticipated touchscreen laptop . Apple’s had a busy few months, launching the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max in September alongside the Apple Watch Series 12 , Apple Watch Ultra 4 and the AirPods 5 , followed by the iPhone Duo going on sale at the end of last week. Apple’s refreshed smart home lineup , revealed during its recent Welcome Home event, is up next: the HomePod Mini 2 will launch on Friday; the Apple HomeView and Apple TV 4K on Nov. 13; and availability for the Home Collection products begins in December. This week will culminate with Apple hosting a special event on Wednesday, and CNET will be on the ground capturing all the latest details. We’ll update this article as more details are revealed. Announced on Monday, Apple’s new iPad Mini is available to preorder on Wednesday and will go on sale Nov. 6. It starts at $699 for 128GB of storage, $799 for 256GB and $999 for 512GB. Setting it apart from the last iPad Mini , which came out two years ago, the new tablet has an 8.5-inch OLED screen (versus an LCD), IP67 water and dust resistance, an Apple A20 processor, a repositioned front-facing camera and a through-screen speaker system called Acoustic Display, as well as being thinner and lighter than before. The latest iMac, announced Tuesday, features Apple’s M6 processor with a CPU and a GPU each having up to 12 cores, two more cores apiece than before, Apple said. A new dual 16-core Neural Engine delivers AI compute that’s up to twice as fast as the previous generation, the company said. The iMac also has a 24-inch 4.5K Retina display. Preorders for the iMac M6 will begin Wednesday, Oct. 28, with availability to follow on Nov. 6. Pricing starts at $1,499 for an iMac with M6 featuring a 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU. It’s available in seven colors: blue, green, pink, yellow, purple, orange and silver. The new 14-inch MacBook Pro, also announced Tuesday, similarly features the M6 processor with 12-core CPU and GPU and dual 16-core Neural Engine for AI tasks. Apple says the battery life runs up to 24 hours. The laptop features a Liquid Retina XDR display, a 12-megapixel Center Stage camera and a six-speaker sound system. The MacBook Pro with M6 can be preordered starting Wednesday, Oct. 28, and will be in stores and delivered to customers starting Nov. 6. Pricing starts at $1,999. Tuesday also brought updates to the Apple Creator Studio software suite. For instance, Final Cut Pro for Mac now includes built-in MotionVFX, a collection of visual effects, plug-ins, transitions, templates and motion graphics tools; the curated Content Hub now includes video assets and is available in Final Cut Pro; Pixelmator Pro introduces Generate Fill, which lets creators transform selected areas of an image using natural language; and Keynote, Pages and Numbers introduce new AI features in beta, including assistants that understand document contexts. The Apple Creator Studio updates will be available in November to subscribers for free. And as for the iPhone Duo launch last week, check out CNET’s ongoing folding test — you can watch the livestream here and tune in on Tuesday as we continue testing how many times the iPhone Duo can fold without cracking in the CNET lab. © 2026 CNET, a Ziff Davis company. All rights reserved.
