sources.title: Apple Is Reportedly Launching a New MacBook Ultra in Fall 2026 With the First-Ever Mac Touchscreen - Hypebeast
passages: Expected to launch in Fall 2026, the MacBook Ultra features a thinner chassis and a 14-inch and 16-inch OLED display .
The redesigned machine incorporates the first touchscreen ever released on a Mac.
Powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, the hardware also integrates a Dynamic Island to align with the modern visual language of the brand.
Apple plans to keep miniLED display panels in production through 2028.

Apple is executing a deliberate bifurcation strategy by retaining the older miniLED MacBook Pro design, which maintains a lower barrier to entry for professional models without pricing out the existing user base.
Reporting from Bloomberg indicates that certain design elements from the premium MacBook Ultra eventually migrate down to these standard professional models.
This strategy allows Apple to keep base professional laptops at a $2,499 entry point while launching the Ultra at a projected $2,999 USD premium
Apple may find OLED middle-ground between MacBook Pro and Air in 2029

coreStoryFacts.text: We’re here on the ground, looking forward to touching those MacBooks (and all the other new Apple products) as we go hands-on.
At an event in Los Angeles, Apple is expected to debut a revamped MacBook Pro with a touchscreen display.
Touchscreen laptops are something Apple executives have criticized for about as long as the iPad has existed.
Some of our remote colleagues will be hanging out in the live blog, too.
This is a very different event than what you might expect at an iPhone launch or WWDC.
Apple's virtual "Peek Performance" event kicks off today at 10:00 a.m.
Pacific Time, where we're expecting to see new iPhone SE and iPad Air models, as well as at least one new Mac model.
Apple is providing a live video stream on its website, on YouTube , and in the company's TV app across its platforms.
We will also be updating this article with live blog coverage and issuing Twitter updates through our @MacRumorsLive account as the keynote unfolds.
Highlights from the event and separate news stories regarding today's announcements will go out through our @MacRumors account.

Live blog transcript ahead... 9:01 am : One hour until showtime!
10:17 am : The M1 Apple Silicon chip is coming to ‌iPad Air‌, same as iPad Pro .
10:07 am : Apple is launching two new finishes for the iPhone 13.
Get weekly top MacRumors stories in your inbox.
As usual, Apple's online store is currently down in advance of the event.
Whether you're upgrading from an older iPhone or completely new to Apple, this guide will help you get the most out your new device.

But there’s more to come: We’re also expecting a long-anticipated touchscreen laptop .
This week will culminate with Apple hosting a special event on Wednesday, and CNET will be on the ground capturing all the latest details.
We’ll update this article as more details are revealed.
13; and availability for the Home Collection products begins in December.
It starts at $699 for 128GB of storage, $799 for 256GB and $999 for 512GB.
The iMac also has a 24-inch 4.5K Retina display.

extraction.body: On Monday, it announced a new iPad Mini with an upgraded OLED display, and on Tuesday, we got M6 chip upgrades for the MacBook Pro and iMac. At an event in Los Angeles, Apple is expected to debut a revamped MacBook Pro with a touchscreen display. This would be the first touchscreen on a Mac (not counting the beleaguered Touch Bar). Touchscreen laptops are something Apple executives have criticized for about as long as the iPad has existed. But after all this time, Apple is expected to give in to the growing demand to let people tap and swipe at a MacBook screen. We’re here on the ground, looking forward to touching those MacBooks (and all the other new Apple products) as we go hands-on. This is a very different event than what you might expect at an iPhone launch or WWDC. For one, we’re at an event space in Los Angeles, not Apple Park in Cupertino. And there are just two of us here from The Verge — yours truly and our video producer Owen Grove. Some of our remote colleagues will be hanging out in the live blog, too. Today is expected to be a lot like the MacBook Neo launch earlier this year in New York City, which had an in-person-only keynote presentation lasting less than 10 minutes before we were unleashed in the hands-on area.

For instance, Final Cut Pro for Mac now includes built-in MotionVFX, a collection of visual effects, plug-ins, transitions, templates and motion graphics tools; the curated Content Hub now includes video assets and is available in Final Cut Pro; Pixelmator Pro introduces Generate Fill, which lets creators transform selected areas of an image using natural language; and Keynote, Pages and Numbers introduce new AI features in beta, including assistants that understand document contexts. The Apple Creator Studio updates will be available in November to subscribers for free. passages: Expected to launch in Fall 2026, the MacBook Ultra features a thinner chassis and a 14-inch and 16-inch OLED display .
The redesigned machine incorporates the first touchscreen ever released on a Mac.
Powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, the hardware also integrates a Dynamic Island to align with the modern visual language of the brand.
Apple plans to keep miniLED display panels in production through 2028.

Apple is executing a deliberate bifurcation strategy by retaining the older miniLED MacBook Pro design, which maintains a lower barrier to entry for professional models without pricing out the existing user base.
Reporting from Bloomberg indicates that certain design elements from the premium MacBook Ultra eventually migrate down to these standard professional models.
This strategy allows Apple to keep base professional laptops at a $2,499 entry point while launching the Ultra at a projected $2,999 USD premium

sources.body: Apple has announced refreshes for the iMac and the entry-level, 14-inch MacBook Pro . Both machines are getting the M6 chip, which was introduced in the Mac mini several weeks ago. In this case, that means up to 30 percent faster graphics and up to double the Neural Engine performance. Apple skipped the M5 and went straight to the M6 here. It caps out at 32GB of RAM but can go to 4TB of storage.

extraction.body: Additionally, the N1 chip brings Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. Apple has announced refreshes for the iMac and the entry-level, 14-inch MacBook Pro . Both machines are getting the M6 chip, which was introduced in the Mac mini several weeks ago. The M6 is split into two variants for the iMac. Picking the “M6 chip with two Thunderbolt ports” option gets you a 10-core CPU and a 10-core GPU, whereas picking “M6 chip with four Thunderbolt ports” gets you 12 cores for each, instead. The two-port variant maxes out at 24 GB of RAM and 1TB of storage, whereas the four-port one maxes out at 32GB of RAM and 2TB of storage. There’s only one M6 chip option for the MacBook Pro—the one with the 12-core GPU and CPU. It caps out at 32GB of RAM but can go to 4TB of storage. It’s a more substantial refresh for the iMac, as its previous update introduced the M4. Apple skipped the M5 and went straight to the M6 here. In terms of performance gains moving from the M4 to the M6, Apple said with the Mac mini that users can expect up to 40 percent faster CPU performance, up to double graphics performance, and nearly five times faster on-device AI. All that largely matches what we saw when we tested the M6 Mac mini last month, and users of the new iMac should expect similar numbers. The M6 iMac should see up to double SSD read/write performance compared to the M4 model, too. The previous entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro had the M5, so that one is just stepping up a single generation. In this case, that means up to 30 percent faster graphics and up to double the Neural Engine performance. In addition to the M6 chip, both computers now have the N1 chip for wireless connectivity (that means Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6). The iMac is now configurable with up to 2.5Gb Ethernet, while the MacBook Pro still lacks an Ethernet port. There are no outward design changes to either device; they both look exactly the same as their immediate predecessors. The iMac starts at $1,499 for the two-port version, or $1,699 for the four-port version. The M6 MacBook Pro starts at $1,999. Preorders start October 28, and they ship November 6. passages: Ahead of its upcoming "Pro and Tell" event, Apple has revealed its refreshed 14-inch MacBook Pro and iMac , powered by its M6 chip.
This means the new MacBook Pro features three Thunderbolt 4 USB-C ports, a MagSafe 3 charging port, a full HDMI port, and an SD card slot.
While this isn't exactly surprising, given Apple's MacBook Pro design has been around for several years now, it would have been nice to see it evolve in some way.
Apple also refreshed its all-in-one iMac with the M6 chip .
This update comes two years after the colorful computer got the M4 chip (the iMac skipped the M5 series entirely).
The base M6 configuration in the iMac features a 10-core CPU and a 10-core GPU, a step up from the 8-core M4 CPU in the last-generation iMac.

Apple says that the M6 features a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, emphasizing that it's a powerful platform for local LLMs and that the chip is designed to take full advantage of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence.
The MacBook M6 also features Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, alongside returning features like the 12-megapixel Center Stage camera and Liquid Retina XDR display with optional nano-texture.
The entry-level iMac starts at $1,500 and will be available to pre-order on October 28th, with shipping starting on November 6th.
Apple also recently revealed its A20-powered iPad mini .
At its upcoming event, the tech giant is expected to show off its long-rumored touchscreen MacBook for the first time.

extraction.body: On the heels of yesterday’s new iPad Mini , Apple has turned its attention to its Mac lineup. Unlike the iPad Mini that received an OLED display and a water-resistant design, today’s Mac updates are mere spec bumps. After debuting its M6 processor with the Mac Mini in August, Apple is bringing the new chip to both its entry-level MacBook Pro and iMac . The M6 chip in the ‌MacBook Pro‌ features a 12-core CPU (two super cores, four performance cores and six efficiency cores) and a 12-core GPU. The previous M5 model had a 10-core CPU (four super cores and six efficiency cores) and a 10-core GPU. In addition, the Neural Engine in the M6 doubles the number of cores, with a dual 16-core NE replacing the single 16-core NE from before. Memory bandwidth also increases from 153GB per second to 170GB per second, but this bump applies only when you choose to outfit the MacBook Pro with 24GB or 32GB of memory, not the default 16GB. Networking improves with support for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, and the new laptop can support dual external 4K displays at up to 165Hz, up from 144Hz. In this era of constantly rising costs , seeing a price remain constant feels like a win. The M6 MacBook Pro starts at the same $1,999 price as the previous model. It’s been nearly two years since the last iMac update, which means Apple’s all-in-one makes the jump from the M4 to the M6 processor. The design (built around a 24-inch, 4.5K Retina display) and color options (blue, green, pink, yellow, purple, orange and silver) stay the same, as does the $1,499 starting price. But now for that $1,499, the M6 iMac has a 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU along with the dual 16-core Neural Engine. That’s up from the M4 chip, which started with eight CPU cores, eight GPU cores and a single 16-core NE. The step-up model costs $1,699 and gets you an M6 chip with a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU, along with four Thunderbolt 4 ports instead of just a pair. This higher-end model also comes with 2.5Gbps Ethernet, which is available as an add-on with the baseline model. The previous M4 iMac offered only gigabit Ethernet. Preorders open Wednesday, Oct. 28, for the new M6 MacBook Pro and M6 iMac, with shipping expected to start on Friday, Nov. 6. Apple’s Pro and Tell week isn’t over. It will culminate with tomorrow’s special event in Los Angeles, where Apple is expected to reveal the long-awaited touchscreen MacBook Pro . © 2026 CNET, a Ziff Davis company. All rights reserved.

sources.title: Apple's M6 chip brings serious on-device AI power to the entry-level MacBook Pro and the colorful iMac - XDA
passages: Ahead of its upcoming "Pro and Tell" event, Apple has revealed its refreshed 14-inch MacBook Pro and iMac , powered by its M6 chip.
This means the new MacBook Pro features three Thunderbolt 4 USB-C ports, a MagSafe 3 charging port, a full HDMI port, and an SD card slot.
While this isn't exactly surprising, given Apple's MacBook Pro design has been around for several years now, it would have been nice to see it evolve in some way.
Apple also refreshed its all-in-one iMac with the M6 chip .
This update comes two years after the colorful computer got the M4 chip (the iMac skipped the M5 series entirely).
The base M6 configuration in the iMac features a 10-core CPU and a 10-core GPU, a step up from the 8-core M4 CPU in the last-generation iMac.

Apple says that the M6 features a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, emphasizing that it's a powerful platform for local LLMs and that the chip is designed to take full advantage of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence.
The MacBook M6 also features Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, alongside returning features like the 12-megapixel Center Stage camera and Liquid Retina XDR display with optional nano-texture.
The entry-level iMac starts at $1,500 and will be available to pre-order on October 28th, with shipping starting on November 6th.
Apple also recently revealed its A20-powered iPad mini .
At its upcoming event, the tech giant is expected to show off its long-rumored touchscreen MacBook for the first time.

Apple’s overhauled MacBook Pro with a touchscreen – coming on Oct 28 – will include a lighter and slightly thinner design, slimmer bezels around the display and OLED technology, Bloomberg reported.

That’s up from the M4 chip, which started with eight CPU cores, eight GPU cores and a single 16-core NE. The M6 chip in the ‌MacBook Pro‌ features a 12-core CPU (two super cores, four performance cores and six efficiency cores) and a 12-core GPU.
It’s been nearly two years since the last iMac update, which means Apple’s all-in-one makes the jump from the M4 to the M6 processor.

passages: Welcome to the Apple 'Pro and Tell' live blog!
I've been combing through the news, leaks and rumors leading up to this event for months now, and we're finally (possibly) at the start of a new paradigm shift for the MacBook Pro!
Apple talked about the new MacBook Pro and iMac.
RAMageddon hit Apple hard earlier this year, as prices of all its computing tech went up by around $2-300.
That puts the iMac at $1,499 and the base model MacBook Pro at $1,999.

For the iMac, Apple didn't say what percent of the total is made with recycled content, but it said it's made with 100% recycled aluminum in the stand, 100% recycled rare earth elements in all magnets, and 100% recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed printed circuit boards.
The window opens at 10:10 am PT on October 28, with a ship date of November 6.
That comes with the Nano-texture display, 32GB of unified memory, 4TB of storage and a 96W power supply.
Yesterday, we saw the iPad mini 8 get announced at 9am ET, and if Apple does something consistently, it's work to patterns.
I'd anticipate an announcement in just under a couple hours time!
Here's how to pre-order the M6 MacBook Pro from Apple and retailers like Amazon and Best Buy.
Apple has announced one new product a day this week.

extraction.body: Forget iPhone Duo and HomeView. This is probably the biggest week of Apple announcements of 2026, as the Cupertino crew looks set to announce a new OLED MacBook Pro with a touchscreen. There's much more too. Apple's already jumped the gun and announced the iPad mini 8 , which makes me think we're getting daily announcements — today we received the M6 MacBook Pro and iMac, with the OLED main event coming Wednesday. And on this live blog, we will cover every single announcement as it happens — exploring every nook and cranny of leaks and rumors and breaking down whether these are the right machines for you. So keep us bookmarked! I've been combing through the news, leaks and rumors leading up to this event for months now, and we're finally (possibly) at the start of a new paradigm shift for the MacBook Pro! I'll walk you through everything. But to kick things off, we got one particularly mini but mighty announcement — an overhauled iPad mini with OLED display . My guess: they're going to slow-play this over the next couple of days leading up to a big fanfare announcement on Wednesday at the actual event in LA. So if the touchscreen Pr-OLED is going to be Wednesday for the big thing, what does that leave? Simple: I'm predicting that today we'll see the M6 iMac and M6 MacBook Pro (base model) announced. I imagine it'll be similar to yesterday's announcement — an update of the Apple Newsroom and a promo video. Keep it locked here for the second it happens at (total prediction) 9am ET. Now, this is where we've not heard much in the rumor mill, so let me take a crack at it. RAMageddon hit Apple hard earlier this year, as prices of all its computing tech went up by around $2-300. That puts the iMac at $1,499 and the base model MacBook Pro at $1,999. These will most probably start at a base memory configuration of 16GB, and these sound like nice, round prices, which I think the Cupertino Crew will keep. I spoke to David Naranjo, Associate Director at Counterpoint Research, who just ran a Bill of Materials (BOM) analysis to see what the price of the OLED MacBook Pro would actually be. Spoiler alert: it's going to get a price hike. Price prediction is "between $2,799 and $2,999." If you're keen to jump on a new MacBook Pro, iPad mini or iMac, there's some good news...ish. The trade-in value of Apple products have gone up! However, does that hint towards a price increase of the new hardware to offset that? We're a little suspicious. Yesterday, we saw the iPad mini 8 get announced at 9am ET, and if Apple does something consistently, it's work to patterns. I'd anticipate an announcement in just under a couple hours time! With the rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro expected to be announced today, we can't help but think about what the first app we'd want to use on a touchscreen MacBook would be. I'm actually writing this post on a MacBook, and I can't think of any particular app in its current form that would be better with a touchscreen. The current macOS design doesn't really need a touchscreen, since it works well with a mouse cursor and keyboard shortcuts. It'll be interesting to see how Apple sells the touchscreen and what use cases it presents during its event. Sure, artists will benefit from drawing on screen with an Apple Pencil, but will other MacBook Pro users really see a reason to pay extra for a touchscreen model? We'll see. Apple talked about the new MacBook Pro and iMac. "The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple's ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030," the company wrote in a news post. For the M6 MacBook Pro, Apple said it used 45% recycled content overall. For the iMac, Apple didn't say what percent of the total is made with recycled content, but it said it's made with 100% recycled aluminum in the stand, 100% recycled rare earth elements in all magnets, and 100% recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed printed circuit boards. If you're curious about just how powerful the M6 is, here are the benchmark results from testing in the Mac mini M6. Obviously, we haven't gotten hands-on with the new iMac and MacBook Pro, but seeing how powerful the chip is makes me excited to try them. That comes with the Nano-texture display, 32GB of unified memory, 4TB of storage and a 96W power supply. Read Apple's full news post for a detailed breakdown of what's new. Tomorrow, at Apple's Pro and Tell event we're expecting to get some hands-on time with all the new devices including the rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro. The new 14-inch and 16-inch models use M5 Pro or M5 Max, with US prices starting at $2,899. Called PROLED XDR, the display supports touch input and brings the Dynamic Island to Mac. Apple lists preorders from October 28, with the first deliveries and shop availability beginning November 6. The touchscreen models join products Apple announced earlier this week: the M6 MacBook Pro and M6 iMac on October 27, and the OLED iPad mini on October 26. Those earlier announcements remain separate from today’s new MacBook Pro. Apple announced the M6 iMac ahead of the October 28 gathering. Image: Apple The 14-inch version with M5 Pro starts at $2,899 in the US, while the 16-inch M5 Pro version starts at $3,399. M5 Max configurations begin at $4,499 and $4,799 respectively. Apple’s announcement also confirms three Thunderbolt 5 ports and storage options up to 16TB. The standard 14-inch M5 Pro configuration has a 15-core CPU, 16-core GPU, 24GB of memory and 1TB of storage. Apple offers the PROLED machines separately from the M6 MacBook Pro with its mini-LED screen. The PROLED models have 14.2-inch and 16.3-inch screens, with refresh rates ranging from 10Hz to 120Hz. Both support P3 and Adobe RGB colour spaces. The brightness rating reaches 2,000 nits for peak HDR and SDR output, while sustained full-screen brightness tops out at 1,000 nits. macOS translates touches into clicks, so Apple says many existing apps work with the touchscreen immediately. Dedicated touch updates for apps including Microsoft Office, Adobe Lightroom and DaVinci Resolve are due later this year. Dynamic Island shows activities and music controls above your work. The lighter designs start at 3lb for the 14-inch model and 4lb for the 16-inch model, with weight varying by configuration. Connectivity includes Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, HDMI, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe 3 and a headphone jack alongside Thunderbolt 5. The upcoming event is called “ Pro and Tell ” and is scheduled for today, October 28, in Los Angeles. This time, Apple is set to focus heavily on its Mac lineup, and the company has already made a couple of major product announcements leading up to the event. Unlike Apple’s traditional launch events, Pro and Tell is expected to be an all-day hands-on gathering for selected members of the press rather than a typical keynote. On top of that, Apple is expected to introduce its new products through announcements and potentially short videos during the day. Apple’s Pro and Tell event will begin today, on October 28, at 10 AM Pacific Time. If you’re wondering how that looks in your region, we’ve put together a list of time zone conversions below. Plus, a countdown clock (which will disappear once it expires). Since this isn’t expected to be a traditional livestreamed keynote, there may not be a single presentation to watch from beginning to end. Instead, announcements could start appearing once the event gets underway. The biggest announcement could be a major MacBook Pro redesign with the rumored MacBook Pro Touch . Apple is reportedly preparing new 14-inch and 16-inch models with OLED displays and touchscreen support, which would bring the latter technology to the Mac for the first time. The laptops could also replace the familiar display notch with a Dynamic Island-style camera area while becoming lighter than the current models. Interestingly, these higher-end MacBook Pros are expected to stick with M5 Pro and M5 Max chips rather than moving to M6 Pro and M6 Max. Meanwhile, the entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro has already received the newer base M6 chip without getting the same major redesign, as announced yesterday. The 24-inch iMac is another device that could receive an M6 upgrade. In this case, however, the processor may be the main change, with the overall design expected to remain largely familiar. coreStoryFacts.text: Apple’s “Pro and tell” event kicks off at 1PM ET / 10AM PT on October 28th.
The event comes just a couple of weeks after Apple debuted the HomeView, its first smart display, and a little over a month after it announced the iPhone Duo, its first foldable.
This event will also continue a streak of product launches at Apple since John Ternus took over as its CEO on September 1st.
Its next event could feature yet another first for Apple: a MacBook with a touchscreen.
So far, the flurry of new devices has also included the iPhone 18 Pro, new Apple Watches, the AirPods 5, and the HomePod Mini 2.
Apple announced an updated iPad Mini with a larger OLED display on Monday.
Welcome to the Apple 'Pro and Tell' live blog!
I've been combing through the news, leaks and rumors leading up to this event for months now, and we're finally (possibly) at the start of a new paradigm shift for the MacBook Pro!
Apple talked about the new MacBook Pro and iMac.
RAMageddon hit Apple hard earlier this year, as prices of all its computing tech went up by around $2-300.
That puts the iMac at $1,499 and the base model MacBook Pro at $1,999.

For the iMac, Apple didn't say what percent of the total is made with recycled content, but it said it's made with 100% recycled aluminum in the stand, 100% recycled rare earth elements in all magnets, and 100% recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed printed circuit boards.
The window opens at 10:10 am PT on October 28, with a ship date of November 6.
That comes with the Nano-texture display, 32GB of unified memory, 4TB of storage and a 96W power supply.
Yesterday, we saw the iPad mini 8 get announced at 9am ET, and if Apple does something consistently, it's work to patterns.
I'd anticipate an announcement in just under a couple hours time!
Here's how to pre-order the M6 MacBook Pro from Apple and retailers like Amazon and Best Buy.
Apple has announced one new product a day this week.
With the rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro expected to be announced today, we can't help but think about what the first app we'd want to use on a touchscreen MacBook would be.
It'll be interesting to see how Apple sells the touchscreen and what use cases it presents during its event.
The trade-in value of Apple products have gone up!
However, does that hint towards a price increase of the new hardware to offset that?
M6 iMac (Announced today): Same design as before, but with M6 inside.
The Pro and Tell gathering was scheduled for 10am Pacific in Los Angeles .

The event comes just a couple of weeks after Apple debuted the HomeView, its first smart display, and a little over a month after it announced the iPhone Duo, its first foldable.
This event will also continue a streak of product launches at Apple since John Ternus took over as its CEO on September 1st.
Its next event could feature yet another first for Apple: a MacBook with a touchscreen.
So far, the flurry of new devices has also included the iPhone 18 Pro, new Apple Watches, the AirPods 5, and the HomePod Mini 2.
Apple announced an updated iPad Mini with a larger OLED display on Monday.

sources.title: Apple event LIVE: MacBook Pro M6 and iMac M6 just announced ahead of 'Pro and Tell' - Yahoo Tech
passages: Welcome to the Apple 'Pro and Tell' live blog!
I've been combing through the news, leaks and rumors leading up to this event for months now, and we're finally (possibly) at the start of a new paradigm shift for the MacBook Pro!
Apple talked about the new MacBook Pro and iMac.
RAMageddon hit Apple hard earlier this year, as prices of all its computing tech went up by around $2-300.
That puts the iMac at $1,499 and the base model MacBook Pro at $1,999.

For the iMac, Apple didn't say what percent of the total is made with recycled content, but it said it's made with 100% recycled aluminum in the stand, 100% recycled rare earth elements in all magnets, and 100% recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed printed circuit boards.
The window opens at 10:10 am PT on October 28, with a ship date of November 6.
That comes with the Nano-texture display, 32GB of unified memory, 4TB of storage and a 96W power supply.
Yesterday, we saw the iPad mini 8 get announced at 9am ET, and if Apple does something consistently, it's work to patterns.
I'd anticipate an announcement in just under a couple hours time!
Here's how to pre-order the M6 MacBook Pro from Apple and retailers like Amazon and Best Buy.
Apple has announced one new product a day this week.
With the rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro expected to be announced today, we can't help but think about what the first app we'd want to use on a touchscreen MacBook would be.
It'll be interesting to see how Apple sells the touchscreen and what use cases it presents during its event.
The trade-in value of Apple products have gone up!
However, does that hint towards a price increase of the new hardware to offset that?
M6 iMac (Announced today): Same design as before, but with M6 inside.

extraction.body: Forget iPhone Duo and HomeView. This is probably the biggest week of Apple announcements of 2026, as the Cupertino crew looks set to announce a new OLED MacBook Pro with a touchscreen. There's much more too. Apple's already jumped the gun and announced the iPad mini 8 , which makes me think we're getting daily announcements — today we received the M6 MacBook Pro and iMac, with the OLED main event coming Wednesday. And on this live blog, we will cover every single announcement as it happens — exploring every nook and cranny of leaks and rumors and breaking down whether these are the right machines for you. So keep us bookmarked! M6 MacBook Pro : 14-inch Liquid Retina XDR display, up to 24 hours of battery life, Powerful M6 chip, Pre-ordering starts Wednesday, October 28 M6 MacBook Pro (Announced today): Same mini-LED design you're used to, but with M6 inside. M6 iMac (Announced today): Same design as before, but with M6 inside. OLED touchscreen MacBook Pro (PREDICTED ANNOUNCEMENT WEDNESDAY): OLED touchscreen, Dynamic Island, M5 Pro/Max. Predicted starting price $2,999 Welcome to the Apple 'Pro and Tell' live blog! I've been combing through the news, leaks and rumors leading up to this event for months now, and we're finally (possibly) at the start of a new paradigm shift for the MacBook Pro! I'll walk you through everything. But to kick things off, we got one particularly mini but mighty announcement — an overhauled iPad mini with OLED display . My guess: they're going to slow-play this over the next couple of days leading up to a big fanfare announcement on Wednesday at the actual event in LA. So if the touchscreen Pr-OLED is going to be Wednesday for the big thing, what does that leave? Simple: I'm predicting that today we'll see the M6 iMac and M6 MacBook Pro (base model) announced. I imagine it'll be similar to yesterday's announcement — an update of the Apple Newsroom and a promo video. Keep it locked here for the second it happens at (total prediction) 9am ET. Now, this is where we've not heard much in the rumor mill, so let me take a crack at it. RAMageddon hit Apple hard earlier this year, as prices of all its computing tech went up by around $2-300. That puts the iMac at $1,499 and the base model MacBook Pro at $1,999. These will most probably start at a base memory configuration of 16GB, and these sound like nice, round prices, which I think the Cupertino Crew will keep. I spoke to David Naranjo, Associate Director at Counterpoint Research, who just ran a Bill of Materials (BOM) analysis to see what the price of the OLED MacBook Pro would actually be. Spoiler alert: it's going to get a price hike. Price prediction is "between $2,799 and $2,999." If you're keen to jump on a new MacBook Pro, iPad mini or iMac, there's some good news...ish. The trade-in value of Apple products have gone up! However, does that hint towards a price increase of the new hardware to offset that? We're a little suspicious. Yesterday, we saw the iPad mini 8 get announced at 9am ET, and if Apple does something consistently, it's work to patterns. I'd anticipate an announcement in just under a couple hours time! With the rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro expected to be announced today, we can't help but think about what the first app we'd want to use on a touchscreen MacBook would be. I'm actually writing this post on a MacBook, and I can't think of any particular app in its current form that would be better with a touchscreen. The current macOS design doesn't really need a touchscreen, since it works well with a mouse cursor and keyboard shortcuts. It'll be interesting to see how Apple sells the touchscreen and what use cases it presents during its event. Sure, artists will benefit from drawing on screen with an Apple Pencil, but will other MacBook Pro users really see a reason to pay extra for a touchscreen model? We'll see. Apple talked about the new MacBook Pro and iMac. "The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple's ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030," the company wrote in a news post. For the M6 MacBook Pro, Apple said it used 45% recycled content overall. For the iMac, Apple didn't say what percent of the total is made with recycled content, but it said it's made with 100% recycled aluminum in the stand, 100% recycled rare earth elements in all magnets, and 100% recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed printed circuit boards. If you're curious about just how powerful the M6 is, here are the benchmark results from testing in the Mac mini M6. Obviously, we haven't gotten hands-on with the new iMac and MacBook Pro, but seeing how powerful the chip is makes me excited to try them. I went to Apple's purchase page and played with the configurations for the M6 MacBook Pro and it appears that most expensive model you can get is $4,069. That comes with the Nano-texture display, 32GB of unified memory, 4TB of storage and a 96W power supply. This news isn't getting as much attention, since new hardware tends to get the most attention: Apple announced a Creator Studio update that adds MotionVFX content to Final Cut Pro, video assets to the Content Hub, expanded music creation tools in Logic Pro, and new intelligence features in Logic Pro, Keynote, Pages, and Numbers. Read Apple's full news post for a detailed breakdown of what's new. Tomorrow, at Apple's Pro and Tell event we're expecting to get some hands-on time with all the new devices including the rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro. Is there anything you're curious about or want us to check out? Let us know in the comments. Apple announced the M6 MacBook Pro today, but it's not up for pre-order just yet. The window opens at 10:10 am PT on October 28, with a ship date of November 6. Here's how to pre-order the M6 MacBook Pro from Apple and retailers like Amazon and Best Buy. Apple has announced one new product a day this week. Just in case you missed it, yesterday was the updated iPad mini 8 .

passages: The Pro and Tell gathering was scheduled for 10am Pacific in Los Angeles .
Apple’s Events page still shows its earlier iPhone presentation at this update; the new hardware details are published on Apple Newsroom .
Apple has announced a touchscreen MacBook Pro with a tandem OLED display at its October 28 product launch.
The new 14-inch and 16-inch models use M5 Pro or M5 Max, with US prices starting at $2,899.
The touchscreen models join products Apple announced earlier this week: the M6 MacBook Pro and M6 iMac on October 27, and the OLED iPad mini on October 26.
Those earlier announcements remain separate from today’s new MacBook Pro.
M5 Max configurations begin at $4,499 and $4,799 respectively.
Apple’s announcement also confirms three Thunderbolt 5 ports and storage options up to 16TB.
Apple lists preorders from October 28, with the first deliveries and shop availability beginning November 6.
Apple gives all three a November 6 launch date.
Delivery estimates for a particular configuration are shown when ordering.
macOS translates touches into clicks, so Apple says many existing apps work with the touchscreen immediately.
Dedicated touch updates for apps including Microsoft Office, Adobe Lightroom and DaVinci Resolve are due later this year.

extraction.body: Apple has announced a touchscreen MacBook Pro with a tandem OLED display at its October 28 product launch. The new 14-inch and 16-inch models use M5 Pro or M5 Max, with US prices starting at $2,899. Called PROLED XDR, the display supports touch input and brings the Dynamic Island to Mac. Apple lists preorders from October 28, with the first deliveries and shop availability beginning November 6. The touchscreen models join products Apple announced earlier this week: the M6 MacBook Pro and M6 iMac on October 27, and the OLED iPad mini on October 26. Those earlier announcements remain separate from today’s new MacBook Pro. Apple announced the M6 iMac ahead of the October 28 gathering. Image: Apple The 14-inch version with M5 Pro starts at $2,899 in the US, while the 16-inch M5 Pro version starts at $3,399. M5 Max configurations begin at $4,499 and $4,799 respectively. Apple’s announcement also confirms three Thunderbolt 5 ports and storage options up to 16TB. The standard 14-inch M5 Pro configuration has a 15-core CPU, 16-core GPU, 24GB of memory and 1TB of storage. Apple offers the PROLED machines separately from the M6 MacBook Pro with its mini-LED screen. The PROLED models have 14.2-inch and 16.3-inch screens, with refresh rates ranging from 10Hz to 120Hz. Both support P3 and Adobe RGB colour spaces. The brightness rating reaches 2,000 nits for peak HDR and SDR output, while sustained full-screen brightness tops out at 1,000 nits. macOS translates touches into clicks, so Apple says many existing apps work with the touchscreen immediately. Dedicated touch updates for apps including Microsoft Office, Adobe Lightroom and DaVinci Resolve are due later this year. Dynamic Island shows activities and music controls above your work. The lighter designs start at 3lb for the 14-inch model and 4lb for the 16-inch model, with weight varying by configuration. Connectivity includes Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, HDMI, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe 3 and a headphone jack alongside Thunderbolt 5. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 , announced on October 27, starts at $1,999 in the US. It has a 12-core CPU, 12-core GPU, Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, with a Liquid Retina XDR display. US preorders are open . The M6 iMac was also announced on October 27. It starts at $1,499 in the US with a 10-core CPU and GPU; the 12-core version starts at $1,699. It retains a 24-inch 4.5K display and comes in seven colours. The new iPad mini was announced on October 26. It combines an 8.5-inch OLED screen with A20 Pro and a landscape front camera. US pricing begins at $699 for Wi-Fi or $849 for cellular, and preorders are open . Apple gives all three a November 6 launch date. Delivery estimates for a particular configuration are shown when ordering. The Pro and Tell gathering was scheduled for 10am Pacific in Los Angeles . Apple’s Events page still shows its earlier iPhone presentation at this update; the new hardware details are published on Apple Newsroom . extraction.body: Apple is preparing to hold another event this month, just a few weeks after its Welcome Home showcase. The upcoming event is called “ Pro and Tell ” and is scheduled for today, October 28, in Los Angeles. This time, Apple is set to focus heavily on its Mac lineup, and the company has already made a couple of major product announcements leading up to the event. Unlike Apple’s traditional launch events, Pro and Tell is expected to be an all-day hands-on gathering for selected members of the press rather than a typical keynote. On top of that, Apple is expected to introduce its new products through announcements and potentially short videos during the day. Apple’s Pro and Tell event will begin today, on October 28, at 10 AM Pacific Time. If you’re wondering how that looks in your region, we’ve put together a list of time zone conversions below. Plus, a countdown clock (which will disappear once it expires). Since this isn’t expected to be a traditional livestreamed keynote, there may not be a single presentation to watch from beginning to end. Instead, announcements could start appearing once the event gets underway. The biggest announcement could be a major MacBook Pro redesign with the rumored MacBook Pro Touch . Apple is reportedly preparing new 14-inch and 16-inch models with OLED displays and touchscreen support, which would bring the latter technology to the Mac for the first time. The laptops could also replace the familiar display notch with a Dynamic Island-style camera area while becoming lighter than the current models. Interestingly, these higher-end MacBook Pros are expected to stick with M5 Pro and M5 Max chips rather than moving to M6 Pro and M6 Max. Meanwhile, the entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro has already received the newer base M6 chip without getting the same major redesign, as announced yesterday. The 24-inch iMac is another device that could receive an M6 upgrade. In this case, however, the processor may be the main change, with the overall design expected to remain largely familiar. Finally, Apple has already introduced a new OLED iPad mini . It’s powered by the same A20 Pro chip found in the iPhone 18 Pro & Pro Max, as well as the iPhone Duo. Despite upgrading to OLED, it’s still only locked to a 60Hz refresh rate . extraction.body: Apple’s smallest tablet is getting a bigger screen. Earlier this week, the company announced the eighth-generation iPad Mini alongside several new MacBook Pro models, bringing OLED technology to Apple’s miniature tablet for the first time. The diminutive slate won’t hit shelves until November 6th; however, you can already preorder it from Amazon, Walmart, Apple, and other retailers in multiple colors starting at $699. The forthcoming iPad Mini features an 8.5-inch OLED display, the largest screen the Mini has ever had, despite being both thinner and lighter than its 2024 predecessor. It also runs on Apple’s new A20 Pro chip, which should deliver faster performance while supporting some of Apple’s new Siri AI features, including the ability to customize Siri’s voice. Apple has also introduced what it calls an “Acoustic Display,” which pairs speakers with the screen and frame to deliver louder, richer sound with deeper bass and clearer highs. The new Mini also features Apple’s N1 wireless networking chip, which adds support for Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. Cellular models additionally get Apple’s new C2 modem, which promises up to 50 percent faster cellular speeds than the previous generation. Upgrading to the 256GB model at any of the aforementioned retailers will cost an additional $100, while the 512GB version will run you $999; the latter also features a more powerful six-core CPU, rather than the five-core CPU in the lower-storage models. If you want cellular connectivity, the 128GB model is available for preorder starting at $849, while the 256GB and 512GB versions cost $949 and $1,149, respectively. Apple also offers a glare-reducing nano-texture display option on the 256GB and 512GB models, starting at $899 and $1,099, respectively.

extraction.body: Ahead of its big "Pro and tell" event on October 28, Apple has pulled back the curtain on its first product reveal of the week: its next-generation iPad mini. Apple calls the new iPad mini its "biggest update ever" to the device, and it's easy to see why. For starters, Apple has increased the screen size to 8.5 inches and upgraded the display from LCD to OLED. That means double the brightness, higher contrast, more vivid colors, and deeper blacks than the previous-gen iPad mini . However, something is still missing: ProMotion, meaning it has only a 60Hz refresh rate. Under the hood, Apple has also upgraded the iPad mini's chipset to the A20 Pro. According to the company, the new chip delivers 4.5x faster AI performance than the previous-gen iPad mini with the A17 Pro chip, along with 2.7x faster graphics performance and up to 60 percent faster multithreaded performance, which will help with tasks like editing photos and videos. Apple has set the new iPad mini's starting price at $700 for the 128GB model, a $100 increase over the previous-gen iPad mini with the A17 Pro, which started at $600. It's also available in a 256GB storage variant priced at $800 and a 512GB model at $900. The Wi-Fi + Cellular model starts at $850. It's available in two colors: Midnight and Starlight. Pre-orders for the new iPad mini are set to begin on October 28 at 10:10 a.m. PT / 1:10 p.m. ET, with the tablet officially launching on November 6. Beyond its upgraded OLED display and A20 Pro chipset, Apple has packed in several other upgrades to help the new iPad mini stand out. Starting with the design, Apple says the new iPad mini is its slimmest and lightest yet, measuring just 5.4 mm thick and weighing 0.56 pounds (255 grams). For comparison, the previous-gen iPad mini measured 6.3 mm thick and weighed 0.65 pounds (293 grams). That means Apple has shaved almost a full millimeter off its thickness while trimming a little weight, too. Apple has also upgraded the front-facing camera to a 12-megapixel landscape camera, the same change it made to the iPad Air and iPad Pro . However, it doesn't support Face ID, and Apple is once again relying on Touch ID for the new iPad mini. On the back, it features a 12-megapixel wide camera. On the connectivity front, the new iPad mini features Apple's N1 networking chip, bringing support for Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. The cellular model also includes Apple's C1X modem for 5G connectivity. Finally, Apple has equipped the new iPad mini with an Acoustic Display system rather than traditional landscape stereo speakers. According to Apple, the system uses "specially designed woofers" paired through the display to deliver punchier bass and higher volume. Overall, I'm impressed by the new iPad mini. Its OLED display should make a huge difference for watching videos, playing games, and editing photos, while the A20 Pro chip should make it an extremely fast little tablet. I just really wish Apple had included ProMotion, which would let the display reach a 120Hz refresh rate. For now, that still seems to be something Apple is keeping exclusive to the iPad Pro. The new iPad mini starts at $700 and launches on November 6, with pre-orders opening this Wednesday, October 28. We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful. The best of Pocket-lint, directly in your inbox.

sources.title: Apple's OLED iPad Mini Launch Set for October Amid Price Surge
passages: Apple is gearing up to launch an OLED-equipped iPad Mini as soon as October, marking the biggest hardware refresh for the compact tablet since its 2021 redesign.
Mark Gurman, who's been tracking Apple's OLED transition for months, first reported last year that the iPad Mini would make the jump with an accompanying price bump.
The company's rumored OLED iPad Mini, slated for an October reveal according to Bloomberg, represents the latest chapter in Cupertino's strategy to premiumize every corner of its product portfolio.
But they also give Apple justification to push the Mini's starting price even higher than the recent $100 increase.

CEO Tim Cook attributed the increases to rising component costs and expanded RAM configurations, but the moves signaled something bigger: Apple's confidence that its ecosystem lock-in gives it pricing power competitors can't match.
Apple's product segmentation has always been precise - each device occupying a specific price band without cannibalizing siblings.
The current iPad Mini, still running a Liquid Retina LCD display, jumped $100 overnight.
That's not a standalone move - it's part of Apple's systematic margin expansion as hardware growth slows.
The iPad Pro got OLED earlier this year with tandem display technology that stacks two OLED panels for exceptional brightness.
Just last month, Apple raised prices across nearly everything it sells - MacBooks, iPads, Macs, even the Vision Pro.
Services revenue, which includes AppleCare, has become critical to Wall Street's Apple narrative.
The iPhone adopted OLED years ago, starting with the iPhone X in 2017.
For shoppers, it means deciding whether OLED's visual pop justifies what could be a $700-plus entry point for a device that once competed on affordability.
Apple is betting consumers will pay more for better screens.
And it's coming at a time when Apple has already shown it's willing to test how much more customers will tolerate.
OLED displays cost more to manufacture - they're thinner, offer better contrast ratios, and enable true blacks that LCDs can't replicate.
Adding OLED could push that north of $700, territory that starts competing with the base iPad Air.
For consumers, the calculus is simple: better screens cost more, and Apple knows you'll pay it.

An OLED panel would represent the first major hardware evolution in five years, transforming the Mini from a budget-friendly option into a premium compact tablet.

Adding OLED could push that north of $700, territory that starts competing with the base iPad Air.

Services revenue, which includes AppleCare, has become critical to Wall Street's Apple narrative.

An OLED display makes that package even more compelling, especially for content consumption where screen quality matters most.
But the pricing pressure reveals Apple's broader strategy.
As smartphone upgrade cycles lengthen and Mac sales plateau, the company is extracting more revenue per customer rather than chasing market share.
The iPad Mini, long the scrappy underdog of Apple's tablet lineup, is getting the premium treatment whether shoppers asked for it or not.
Apple's OLED iPad Mini isn't just a display upgrade - it's a signal that no product is safe from the company's premiumization playbook.
With prices already up $100 and another increase likely this fall, the Mini is transforming from value option to premium compact.
For Apple, it's a bet that ecosystem loyalty trumps price sensitivity.
For shoppers, it means deciding whether OLED's visual pop justifies what could be a $700-plus entry point for a device that once competed on affordability.
As the last LCD holdouts prepare to make the switch by 2028, one thing is clear: Apple's margin expansion isn't slowing down, and your wallet is footing the bill.

extraction.body: Apple’s smallest tablet is getting a bigger screen. Earlier this week, the company announced the eighth-generation iPad Mini alongside several new MacBook Pro models, bringing OLED technology to Apple’s miniature tablet for the first time. The diminutive slate won’t hit shelves until November 6th; however, you can already preorder it from Amazon, Walmart, Apple, and other retailers in multiple colors starting at $699. The forthcoming iPad Mini features an 8.5-inch OLED display, the largest screen the Mini has ever had, despite being both thinner and lighter than its 2024 predecessor. It also runs on Apple’s new A20 Pro chip, which should deliver faster performance while supporting some of Apple’s new Siri AI features, including the ability to customize Siri’s voice. Apple has also introduced what it calls an “Acoustic Display,” which pairs speakers with the screen and frame to deliver louder, richer sound with deeper bass and clearer highs. The new Mini also features Apple’s N1 wireless networking chip, which adds support for Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. Cellular models additionally get Apple’s new C2 modem, which promises up to 50 percent faster cellular speeds than the previous generation. Upgrading to the 256GB model at any of the aforementioned retailers will cost an additional $100, while the 512GB version will run you $999; the latter also features a more powerful six-core CPU, rather than the five-core CPU in the lower-storage models. If you want cellular connectivity, the 128GB model is available for preorder starting at $849, while the 256GB and 512GB versions cost $949 and $1,149, respectively. Apple also offers a glare-reducing nano-texture display option on the 256GB and 512GB models, starting at $899 and $1,099, respectively.

extraction.body: Ahead of its big "Pro and tell" event on October 28, Apple has pulled back the curtain on its first product reveal of the week: its next-generation iPad mini. Apple calls the new iPad mini its "biggest update ever" to the device, and it's easy to see why. For starters, Apple has increased the screen size to 8.5 inches and upgraded the display from LCD to OLED. That means double the brightness, higher contrast, more vivid colors, and deeper blacks than the previous-gen iPad mini . However, something is still missing: ProMotion, meaning it has only a 60Hz refresh rate. Under the hood, Apple has also upgraded the iPad mini's chipset to the A20 Pro. According to the company, the new chip delivers 4.5x faster AI performance than the previous-gen iPad mini with the A17 Pro chip, along with 2.7x faster graphics performance and up to 60 percent faster multithreaded performance, which will help with tasks like editing photos and videos. Apple has set the new iPad mini's starting price at $700 for the 128GB model, a $100 increase over the previous-gen iPad mini with the A17 Pro, which started at $600. It's also available in a 256GB storage variant priced at $800 and a 512GB model at $900. The Wi-Fi + Cellular model starts at $850. It's available in two colors: Midnight and Starlight. Pre-orders for the new iPad mini are set to begin on October 28 at 10:10 a.m. PT / 1:10 p.m. ET, with the tablet officially launching on November 6. Beyond its upgraded OLED display and A20 Pro chipset, Apple has packed in several other upgrades to help the new iPad mini stand out. Starting with the design, Apple says the new iPad mini is its slimmest and lightest yet, measuring just 5.4 mm thick and weighing 0.56 pounds (255 grams). For comparison, the previous-gen iPad mini measured 6.3 mm thick and weighed 0.65 pounds (293 grams). That means Apple has shaved almost a full millimeter off its thickness while trimming a little weight, too. Apple has also upgraded the front-facing camera to a 12-megapixel landscape camera, the same change it made to the iPad Air and iPad Pro . However, it doesn't support Face ID, and Apple is once again relying on Touch ID for the new iPad mini. On the back, it features a 12-megapixel wide camera. On the connectivity front, the new iPad mini features Apple's N1 networking chip, bringing support for Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. The cellular model also includes Apple's C1X modem for 5G connectivity. Finally, Apple has equipped the new iPad mini with an Acoustic Display system rather than traditional landscape stereo speakers. According to Apple, the system uses "specially designed woofers" paired through the display to deliver punchier bass and higher volume. Overall, I'm impressed by the new iPad mini. Its OLED display should make a huge difference for watching videos, playing games, and editing photos, while the A20 Pro chip should make it an extremely fast little tablet. I just really wish Apple had included ProMotion, which would let the display reach a 120Hz refresh rate. For now, that still seems to be something Apple is keeping exclusive to the iPad Pro. The new iPad mini starts at $700 and launches on November 6, with pre-orders opening this Wednesday, October 28. We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful. The best of Pocket-lint, directly in your inbox.

It's also available in a 256GB storage variant priced at $800 and a 512GB model at $900. The Wi-Fi + Cellular model starts at $850. It's available in two colors: Midnight and Starlight.
Pre-orders for the new iPad mini are set to begin on October 28 at 10:10 a.m. PT / 1:10 p.m. ET, with the tablet officially launching on November 6.
Beyond its upgraded OLED display and A20 Pro chipset, Apple has packed in several other upgrades to help the new iPad mini stand out.

Starting with the design, Apple says the new iPad mini is its slimmest and lightest yet, measuring just 5.4 mm thick and weighing 0.56 pounds (255 grams). For comparison, the previous-gen iPad mini measured 6.3 mm thick and weighed 0.65 pounds (293 grams). That means Apple has shaved almost a full millimeter off its thickness while trimming a little weight, too.

Apple has also upgraded the front-facing camera to a 12-megapixel landscape camera, the same change it made to the iPad Air and iPad Pro . However, it doesn't support Face ID, and Apple is once again relying on Touch ID for the new iPad mini. On the back, it features a 12-megapixel wide camera.

On the connectivity front, the new iPad mini features Apple's N1 networking chip, bringing support for Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. The cellular model also includes Apple's C1X modem for 5G connectivity.

Finally, Apple has equipped the new iPad mini with an Acoustic Display system rather than traditional landscape stereo speakers. According to Apple, the system uses "specially designed woofers" paired through the display to deliver punchier bass and higher volume.

Overall, I'm impressed by the new iPad mini. Its OLED display should make a huge difference for watching videos, playing games, and editing photos, while the A20 Pro chip should make it an extremely fast little tablet. I just really wish Apple had included ProMotion, which would let the display reach a 120Hz refresh rate. For now, that still seems to be something Apple is keeping exclusive to the iPad Pro.
The new iPad mini starts at $700 and launches on November 6, with pre-orders opening this Wednesday, October 28.

sources.title: Apple's OLED iPad Mini Launch Set for October Amid Price Surge
passages: Apple is gearing up to launch an OLED-equipped iPad Mini as soon as October, marking the biggest hardware refresh for the compact tablet since its 2021 redesign.
Mark Gurman, who's been tracking Apple's OLED transition for months, first reported last year that the iPad Mini would make the jump with an accompanying price bump.
The company's rumored OLED iPad Mini, slated for an October reveal according to Bloomberg, represents the latest chapter in Cupertino's strategy to premiumize every corner of its product portfolio.
But they also give Apple justification to push the Mini's starting price even higher than the recent $100 increase.

CEO Tim Cook attributed the increases to rising component costs and expanded RAM configurations, but the moves signaled something bigger: Apple's confidence that its ecosystem lock-in gives it pricing power competitors can't match.
Apple's product segmentation has always been precise - each device occupying a specific price band without cannibalizing siblings.
The current iPad Mini, still running a Liquid Retina LCD display, jumped $100 overnight.
That's not a standalone move - it's part of Apple's systematic margin expansion as hardware growth slows.
The iPad Pro got OLED earlier this year with tandem display technology that stacks two OLED panels for exceptional brightness.
Just last month, Apple raised prices across nearly everything it sells - MacBooks, iPads, Macs, even the Vision Pro.
Services revenue, which includes AppleCare, has become critical to Wall Street's Apple narrative.
The iPhone adopted OLED years ago, starting with the iPhone X in 2017.
For shoppers, it means deciding whether OLED's visual pop justifies what could be a $700-plus entry point for a device that once competed on affordability.
Apple is betting consumers will pay more for better screens.
And it's coming at a time when Apple has already shown it's willing to test how much more customers will tolerate.
OLED displays cost more to manufacture - they're thinner, offer better contrast ratios, and enable true blacks that LCDs can't replicate.
Adding OLED could push that north of $700, territory that starts competing with the base iPad Air.
For consumers, the calculus is simple: better screens cost more, and Apple knows you'll pay it.

passages: Oct 27 (Reuters) - OpenAI plans to buy Google's AI chips, The Information reported on Tuesday, citing a person familiar with the matter, as technology companies ramp up spending to meet surging demand for AI computing.
OpenAI is already among the largest buyers of Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs), which it uses to train and deploy AI models.
Google began selling TPUs directly to some customers this year.
The reported plan would deepen ties between OpenAI and Alphabet's Google, which compete in AI products and search but have increasingly struck commercial deals.
Last week, OpenAI said it would make its frontier AI models available through Google Cloud.
The report did not disclose financial terms or other details.
Google did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment outside regular business hours, while OpenAI declined to comment.

Alphabet expects to begin recognizing a small percentage of revenue from TPU sales agreements by the end of this year, with the vast majority expected to be recognized in 2027, CFO Anat Ashkenazi previously said.

Amazon, Microsoft and Google parent Alphabet plan to spend as much as $600 billion combined this year on AI infrastructure as investors increasingly question when such spending will translate into meaningful returns.

The potential purchase comes as Google expands its chip business beyond its own cloud platform.

extraction.body: Matt Walsh has opened up about Donald Trump's attempts to officially ban the term "Artificial Intelligence". He wants to replace it with the term "Super Intelligence" or SI. AI, or Artificial Intelligence, has been one of the most prominent terms in recent years with the rise of the technology worldwide. In September this year, Trump met with the tech leaders of numerous companies to discuss potential regulations on AI use in the US. He also said that AI should be replaced with the term SI back then. On Tuesday, October 27, the POTUS shared a post on Truth Social about the change in the term. He said that they will officially ban the term AI, writing: “When will The Wall Street Journal start calling Artificial Intelligence (AI), a very bad and inaccurate name, SI (Super Intelligence), the name which virtually everyone else is using, or soon will be. In short order, we will be officially BANNING the term, ‘AI/Artificial Intelligence,’ in all relevant documents, and everything else, due to its inaccuracy. Thank you for your attention to this matter.” Political commentator Matt Walsh shared his thoughts on this post, writing on X (formerly Twitter) : "I have no idea why renaming AI is so bizarrely important to Trump. Nobody cares about the name he chose. Nobody is using it or will use it. And it’s not even technically accurate because “super intelligence” already had an agreed upon, widely adopted definition. This is the weirdest political hill to die on. It gains you nothing." "Not a single ordinary American in the country, anywhere, cares deeply about making sure people say “SI” instead of “AI.” We are days away from a major election and this bulls**t is the focus? Just baffling," he added. Walsh had also taken a dig at the potential change in the term in September. He wrote in a post that he was "already cringing at the thought of conservatives" using the term "Super Intelligence". Also Read: "Impossible for me to fathom": Matt Walsh reacts after Corie Walsh's husband reportedly supports her in court after she allegedly hanged their child On September 29, Donald Trump hosted the leaders of many big tech companies to discuss potential AI regulations. The likes of Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, and Dario Amodei were all in attendance. After lunch, the POTUS spoke about renaming AI to SI. He also signed an executive order to use "SI" or "Super Intelligence" in government documents. Part of the executive order read: “[T]he term ‘Super Intelligence’ more appropriately captures the promise, potential, and rapidly advancing capabilities of these technologies. It is therefore the policy of my Administration that, to the maximum extent permitted by law, the executive branch shall use the terms ‘Super Intelligence’ and ‘SI’ in place of ‘Artificial Intelligence’ and ‘AI’ and will not acknowledge the usage of ‘Artificial Intelligence’ and ‘AI’ in any applicable setting.” In the order, he claimed that the advancements in this technology "increasingly amplify human ingenuity and unlock new forms of creativity". Hence, it represents "not merely artificial intelligence, but a new era of Super Intelligence." On October 27, US President Donald Trump announced on the social media platform Truth Social that his administration would soon officially ban the use of the term "artificial intelligence" ( AI ), citing a lack of precision in the terminology. "In the near future, we will officially BAN the term 'AI/Artificial Intelligence' in all related documents and everything else due to its inaccuracy," Trump wrote. Instead, the US President wants to standardize the term for this technology as "Super Intelligence" (SI). Mr. Trump also directly criticized the financial newspaper The Wall Street Journal for continuing to use the term AI: "When will The Wall Street Journal start calling Artificial Intelligence (AI) – a very bad and inaccurate name – SI (Super Intelligence), a name that almost everyone else is using or will soon be using?" Earlier in September, President Trump signed an executive order directing agencies under the executive branch to switch to using the acronym SI instead of AI. Speaking at the United Nations General Assembly last month, he also affirmed to world leaders that the US would change the name of this technology in diplomatic documents. "The use of the word 'artificial' makes this intelligence sound artificial. It's not artificial at all; it's truly extraordinary. But we have to be careful. In fact, its nature is quite the opposite of what the word implies," Trump argued. Earlier this month, President Trump announced the creation of a task force called the "Super Intelligence Force," directly led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton. According to the announcement, the organization's mission is to coordinate all federal government efforts to ensure that the United States continues to maintain its leading position in the field of superintelligence – a technological wave that he assessed as "on a scale larger than both the Industrial Revolution and the Internet." This force is tasked with coordinating closely between the federal government and consumers, public interest organizations, religious organizations, critical infrastructure providers, and SI technology development corporations to protect the interests and improve the lives of American citizens.

AI, or Artificial Intelligence, has been one of the most prominent terms in recent years with the rise of the technology worldwide. In September this year, Trump met with the tech leaders of numerous companies to discuss potential regulations on AI use in the US. He also said that AI should be replaced with the term SI back then. On Tuesday, October 27, the POTUS shared a post on Truth Social about the change in the term. He said that they will officially ban the term AI, writing: “When will The Wall Street Journal start calling Artificial Intelligence (AI), a very bad and inaccurate name, SI (Super Intelligence), the name which virtually everyone else is using, or soon will be. In short order, we will be officially BANNING the term, ‘AI/Artificial Intelligence,’ in all relevant documents, and everything else, due to its inaccuracy. Thank you for your attention to this matter.” Political commentator Matt Walsh shared his thoughts on this post, writing on X (formerly Twitter) : "I have no idea why renaming AI is so bizarrely important to Trump. Nobody cares about the name he chose. Nobody is using it or will use it. And it’s not even technically accurate because “super intelligence” already had an agreed upon, widely adopted definition. This is the weirdest political hill to die on. It gains you nothing." "Not a single ordinary American in the country, anywhere, cares deeply about making sure people say “SI” instead of “AI.” We are days away from a major election and this bulls**t is the focus? Just baffling," he added. Walsh had also taken a dig at the potential change in the term in September. He wrote in a post that he was "already cringing at the thought of conservatives" using the term "Super Intelligence". Also Read: "Impossible for me to fathom": Matt Walsh reacts after Corie Walsh's husband reportedly supports her in court after she allegedly hanged their child On September 29, Donald Trump hosted the leaders of many big tech companies to discuss potential AI regulations. The likes of Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, and Dario Amodei were all in attendance. After lunch, the POTUS spoke about renaming AI to SI. He also signed an executive order to use "SI" or "Super Intelligence" in government documents. Part of the executive order read: “[T]he term ‘Super Intelligence’ more appropriately captures the promise, potential, and rapidly advancing capabilities of these technologies. It is therefore the policy of my Administration that, to the maximum extent permitted by law, the executive branch shall use the terms ‘Super Intelligence’ and ‘SI’ in place of ‘Artificial Intelligence’ and ‘AI’ and will not acknowledge the usage of ‘Artificial Intelligence’ and ‘AI’ in any applicable setting.” In the order, he claimed that the advancements in this technology "increasingly amplify human ingenuity and unlock new forms of creativity". Hence, it represents "not merely artificial intelligence, but a new era of Super Intelligence." According to the announcement, the organization's mission is to coordinate all federal government efforts to ensure that the United States continues to maintain its leading position in the field of superintelligence – a technological wave that he assessed as "on a scale larger than both the Industrial Revolution and the Internet." This force is tasked with coordinating closely between the federal government and consumers, public interest organizations, religious organizations, critical infrastructure providers, and SI technology development corporations to protect the interests and improve the lives of American citizens.

extraction.body: Bitwise Asset Management has raised its Bitcoin price target to $1.6 million by 2036, up from its previous forecast of $1.3 million by 2035, citing expanding institutional demand and growing interest in assets that protect against currency debasement. In its latest long term capital market assumptions report , the asset manager projected a compound annual growth rate of 34.3% for Bitcoin over the next decade, compared with the 28.3% annualized return estimated in last year's report. The revised forecast comes despite Bitcoin losing 53% of its value between its October 2025 peak above $125,000 and its June 2026 low below $59,000. Bitwise Chief Investment Officer Matt Hougan said he initially expected the market downturn and deteriorating macroeconomic conditions to force the firm to lower its long term outlook. Instead, the updated model produced a higher valuation, driven primarily by increases in the size of markets that Bitcoin could potentially capture. "Using the exact same model as last year with updated data, we're raising our 10-year forecast from $1.3 million to $1.6 million," Hougan wrote. The asset manager maintained its previous assumptions about Bitcoin's share of each addressable market, meaning the higher target reflects larger market opportunities rather than more aggressive adoption estimates. Bitwise's updated valuation model projects that the global store of value market will reach approximately $110 trillion over the next decade, up from its previous estimate of $91 trillion. The firm also increased its projected institutional investment market from $216 trillion to $303 trillion, reflecting expectations of expanding financial assets and growing institutional demand. According to Hougan, Bitcoin's potential valuation depends on two factors: the total size of the markets it can serve and the share of those markets it ultimately captures. The report identifies store of value assets, institutional investment portfolios, offshore wealth and emerging market currencies among Bitcoin's potential opportunities. Bitwise expects persistent inflation, rising government debt and currency debasement concerns to increase demand for scarce assets over the coming decade. The firm argues that Bitcoin could benefit from these trends as investors seek alternatives to traditional fiat currencies and government debt. Hougan also pointed to growing institutional adoption, including increased access through wealth management platforms such as Wells Fargo and Merrill Lynch. He said central banks and sovereign wealth funds have also moved closer to digital asset exposure, while Bitcoin's historical volatility has gradually declined. Despite these developments, Bitwise kept its market penetration assumptions unchanged from last year's model. The firm estimates that Bitcoin's share of the broader store of value market has already increased from less than 1% a decade ago to more than 5%. The report acknowledges that Bitcoin's recent performance has challenged investor confidence, particularly after its decline from record highs. However, Bitwise argues that the 53% peak to trough loss was considerably smaller than the drawdowns exceeding 80% recorded during previous major Bitcoin bear markets. The company interprets the smaller decline as a possible indication of a maturing market supported by a broader institutional investor base. Hougan also noted that institutional investors continued adding Bitcoin exposure during the downturn, even as exchange traded fund inflows slowed. The report highlights Bitcoin's increasing correlation with gold, although most of the recent demand for traditional store of value assets has flowed into the precious metal rather than cryptocurrencies. Bitwise expects Bitcoin to remain volatile over the coming decade but projects that its price fluctuations will gradually moderate as institutional participation expands. The firm also expects Bitcoin's traditional four year market cycle to become less influential as its investor base grows. Still, the report cautions that significant drawdowns remain possible and identifies regulatory uncertainty, technological disruption and advances in quantum computing as potential risks to its assumptions. Hougan said Bitcoin's ability to maintain institutional interest through a difficult market environment has strengthened his confidence in its longer term prospects. The firm's outlook rests on continued institutional adoption, demand for hard assets and Bitcoin's limited supply. Unlike conventional currencies, Bitcoin has a predetermined issuance schedule and a maximum supply of approximately 21 million coins. Bitwise argues that this supply structure could become increasingly important if demand expands among institutional investors and other large capital allocators. The asset manager expects Bitcoin to outperform major traditional asset classes over the next decade, although its forecast remains dependent on assumptions about market growth and adoption. The report also projects that Bitcoin will maintain relatively low to moderate correlations with stocks, bonds and other major asset categories, potentially supporting its role in diversified investment portfolios. Bitwise emphasized that the $1.6 million valuation is a model based projection rather than a guaranteed price outcome. Select market data provided by ICE Data Services .
